en: Likely the first weapon a Fighter holds. It's called "long" next to the short sword, but isn't really that long. Its length, weight and grip are tuned so even a novice can wield it. It's cheap, but grip it again after using other swords and you'll notice the smith's care. Then you've come of age.

A distinctive sword with a curved, single-edged blade, said to come from a culture apart from straight swords. The curve follows no standard, so lining them up is fun: each smith's fixations and quirks show through. Some collect them as a hobby or use them in guess-the-smith party games.
Perhaps it was once a keen sword, but in this state it can neither cut nor stab. A sword that endured many battles now sleeps quietly with its owner's memories.

By nature it's closer to an axe than a sword: a blade made purely for smashing down. Its swings are easy to read. But just imagine the terror of brawny fighters bringing this sword down on you with all their might.

Improved over and over to merge the strengths of many swords into the ultimate blade, it came full circle back to an ordinary shape. It lacks the star quality first aimed for, but it became a versatile weapon that does what's expected in most situations.

Made of finer ore than a normal long sword, then fired and hammered for three days and nights. The result is a tougher blade than the standard long sword. It looks almost unchanged, but use it once and you'll be amazed at how much better it cuts.

A bit ungainly for a knight to carry. Yet despite its looks, it's no bad sword. Its edge is ground sharp so it can cut. Unlike other swords it is made almost entirely of bone, so it's light and easy to handle.

A sword adventurers dream of. Even at low levels it delivers steady power. But that isn't its only draw: the blade is charged with magic, and one stroke sends a wave of flame rushing at the foe. Once it's yours, the danger to watch for may be not the monsters but your own complacency.

A sword only those who keep to a single path may bear. In an age when anyone can freely change their path, following one path to its end may be hard and harsh. Yet there truly is a view seen only by those who master one path without ever looking aside.

A sword said to hold the power of the wind spirit. It is always wreathed in lightning, and when swung down at a target it calls a mighty thunderbolt from the sky. It's strong as is, but in the hands of one with lightning magic it may do even more.

In every age, some are bewitched by the allure of evil. This sword too was forged by a smith drawn to the dark alignment. It should be made of the same material as a long sword, yet in sharpness and power it became an entirely different blade.
A legendary sword said to unleash more power the older its wielder is. Its wooden blade looks flimsy at first glance, but an unseen force lets it cut even through iron.

A famed sword whose name is carved into legend. Since it became known, many adventurers have tried to get it, but few have been lucky enough. True to a legendary sword, it also has the welcome power to prevent confusion.
Ordinary weapons can't scratch a dragon's huge, hard scales. By specializing against dragons, the Dragon Killer gained the means to pierce their hide. It is unwieldy, so it slightly hampers defense.
A sword only a Lord may own. It's said the unworthy cannot even touch it. Yet its power as a sword is only upper-middle, and some suspect it is a fake.

A lavish sword cut from a huge, long mass of diamond ore, a true miracle of nature. Besides its power it is worth a lot as a gem, so even classes that can't use swords want it to sell. Parties that find it often fall into bloody fights over it.

A sword with a bird-shaped ornament on its hilt. In its center is set a gem named Alverstar, said to lend strength to its wielder. One theory holds that the Alverstar's true worth is this sword's protection.

A blade of sacred power, purified by holy force. Weak demons are said to flee from anyone who merely holds it. It's also said that some who spend time with it turn from Evil to Good. Might its holy light reach even into people's hearts?

A sword made to sever the world of the dead from this one. Its task done, it now sleeps quietly. Its aura is the miasma of the underworld, and its blade is said to show every evil deed of this world. Should one without will wield it, they will be cursed and carried off to the land of the dead.
A sword said to appear when a true Lord rises in the world. Borders no longer matter. Wherever this sword is, there is the kingdom, and whoever holds it is the one, absolute king.
A knife-like weapon that many classes can use, not just fighter types. But it also has the drawback of low power. Unless you're facing lots of enemies, equipping a shield instead may be wiser.
A shorter sword, the long sword's partner. As a sub-weapon for beginners, it's decent.
A short blade known for its bent shape. Used not only as a weapon but often for farming and everyday chores.
A short blade rusted by wind and rain. Nothing remains of how it once looked. It is said misfortune befalls whoever takes it up.

At first glance an ordinary dagger. But fine patterns carved on the blade scatter light, making the tip's movement hard to follow. Those it cuts won't know why they're hurt and will fall into confusion.

Like a chimera, its marbled blade is an alloy of three metals: Dvel Soft Steel, Frozen Elven Iron and Mazurite. It amplifies each ore's magic and guards the owner against "Poison," "Paralysis" and "Silence."
A dagger that has drunk adventurers' blood for ages. Its thirst never ends; it even craves its owner's blood. It is cursed: it sells high, but equip it by mistake and you're in for a nasty time.
This sword is a symbol of beginning and end. It is said only an Alchemist can draw out its true worth.

A short blade made to handle any situation. Used right, the many varied blades that come out of its one sheath make it a powerful weapon. But if you can't master them all, it's a treasure gone to waste. A tricky weapon to handle. ...Weapon?

The ultimate small blade every Thief dreams of. It's first-rate as a weapon, but they say its greatest appeal is its simple design, built for functional beauty. Its gleaming silver edge never chips, and it makes Beastfolk flinch.

A good blade must not break, must not bend, and must cut. The katana has all three to a high degree and excels at killing people and monsters. It's also beautiful. So many want one not only for its sheer fighting power but because they've fallen for its looks.

A blade said to cut down a hundred bamboo leaves in one stroke. Its accuracy is uncannily high, so even a novice Samurai can shine with it. Many Samurai can't part with it even after getting finer katana.

A bold weapon meant to smash the foe's skull right through the helmet. Katana are meant to "cut," but this one works more as a blunt weapon. Unusually for a katana, it is handled like a Western sword.

A katana so famous in a far eastern land that Kogarasumaru became a brand. It was first the name of one katana with a double-edged tip, but later katana of the same make were called Kogarasumaru too. Those sold in this country are made the same way as the original.
Grip the hilt with both hands and swing its long, huge blade, and you'll hear a sound as if the sword were roaring. The poor prey before you can only tremble.

A sacred katana used, along with song and dance, when dedicating a ritual performance to the gods. It is usually enshrined amid nature, deep in forests or by lakes, so its spiritual power is higher than a normal katana's.

To atone for a crime, or to guard one's honor: a samurai at times takes their own life. To spare a dying samurai pain, custom called for an assistant to strike off the head after the self-inflicted cut. This katana long served that role and holds not only grudges but all manner of passions.

A katana that unites sharpness, toughness and beauty at an even higher level is called a masterwork. And this Odenta surely is one. It is said to be sharp enough to cut two people in half at once. An edge that never dulls however many it cuts is also the mark of a masterwork.
Its blade is studded with gemstones, and each swing leaves a ribbon of light in the air. Beautiful though it is, it has the added effect of surely poisoning anyone it cuts.

To samurai this katana's name stirs both longing and dread. The strongest katana in name and deed. Yet many samurai are said to become obsessed with its edge and fall into wickedness. That is why Muramasa is called a cursed blade. What new legend will this storied katana create next?

A standard spear. Any fighter-type class can use it, but its power is low. Its merit is reaching the enemy's back row. It widens toward the grip to shield the hand, lowering the risk of a foe hitting your hand and making you drop the lance when you thrust.

Don't scoff at it as mere cleaning gear. A familiar tool is the best partner. It has a spear's traits too, of course, and back-row attacks are its specialty. Some Servants reportedly keep using the mop even after getting strong weapons.

A long spear with a large triangular head. Built to excel at slashing and thrusting, the functions no weapon can do without, it is a spear made purely for attack. The blade makes up nearly all its weight, so slashes that carry that weight are extremely effective.

A foreign spear painted vermilion all over. Fitting for a weapon that flaunts itself, it performs well. But if its bearer doesn't live up to it, the monsters it draws will gang up and beat them to a pulp.

Kavirane is an old word meaning "the unforgivable" or "eternal sin." They say it comes to those who have long lived keeping the fire of a grudge alive. Take it, and you can settle your grudge, but you too will wander as a spite spear.

A spear made by drawing out rare, precious mithril. Light, sharp and yet sturdy, it truly is an ideal spear. It's easy to strike foes with even from horseback, and you can picture it shining in all sorts of situations.
Fruit grown up high? Harvest it with ease using this! A tool in everyday use on farms and orchards, but handle with care. After all, it has a slight power to behead.
Here lies one possibility. A blade of rebellion, allowed only to those close to the gods. Whether to wield it is up to you. But what awaits beyond will not welcome you.
A spear forged from Frozen Elven Iron and Mazurite. Pale blue all over, it glows softly, flickering in the dark. Its tip is reinforced with frost magic and protects the owner from fire.

A spear said to come only to Valkyries the gods have acknowledged. To a master it accepts, it lends equal strength whatever their skill. Now, battle maidens! Face the darkness and offer the gods your finest dance!
There are many kinds of axe, and their shapes have changed to suit how they were used. In the orthodox sense, 'axe' means a weapon like this hand axe: a wooden haft fitted with a metal blade.
A war axe evolved from the hand axe into a shape more practical in real combat. The blade on its long haft can "cut," "thrust" and "sweep."

Bones of the dead fused together into a great axe. Not even Dispel works on it anymore; it thinks only of absorbing the foes it fells and growing mightier. And when its owner falls, it absorbs them too and awaits its next master.
A hand axe said to belong to giants. But its size is no joke; even a dwarf might not handle it properly. If you get it but doubt your strength, be sensible and hang it on a wall or sell it.
A hammer adjusted for use in battle. It has the traits of a blunt weapon and takes some strength to wield. Its simple appeal, clubbing foes until they drop, makes it popular.

You beat your foe in a frenzy until they're a bloody mess, and before you know it, only a lump of meat lies there. Delighting in the slick feel of the weapon in your grip, you run your fingers over it endlessly, smiling. Do people create the Blood Hammer, or does the Blood Hammer change people?

Deathdeath pikopiko, bloodshed! Deathdeath pikopiko, boom! Hits hurt, My Darling, but don't run, fall in HELL! I'll haunt you anywhere, love's range cap OFF! (zing!) Deathdeath pikopiko, fresh blood! Deathdeath pikopiko, precious! Even burnt to ash, by love's special POW-WER! I L-O-V-E U...smooch~

A very precious hammer made only of pure, unmixed mithril. Nothing can withstand it, and it's a great help in mining too. But given what it's made of, they say it won't pay for itself unless you strike rich veins again and again.

The ultimate hammer, said to be something a demon god left behind. An amateur can't handle it, but if you have a veteran Fighter, by all means give it to them. One swing will make a pile of mincemeat.
This weapon is used mainly by clergy. Clergy are forbidden to use blades that shed others' blood. So they carry the mace, which lets them defend themselves without spilling a foe's blood.
An enhanced mace. It's even deadlier; a priest attacking with it could give you a hard fight. Still, picturing clergy pondering how to kill people more efficiently is a bit comical.

Swords deal damage mainly by cutting, so if the blade can't get through armor, damage inevitably drops. Striking weapons like this one deal damage by impact instead, so they easily hurt even foes covered head to toe in armor.

Use it to save those who have strayed, and they stray even further. Maybe that's why it's called the Mace of Straying. After all, if it could save the lost, it would be named something like the Mace of Salvation. Or maybe the one who's straying is the cleric holding it.

A mace of thin iron plates wound around a thick iron core, the way a snake coils around its prey. The plates are steeped in deadly venom; touching them to a wound inflicts deadly poison. Merely carrying it is also said to grant some resistance to poison.
A mace made with nothing but destruction in mind. Bringing its iron fist down on a target gives the wielder a thrill that simply cannot be beaten.

A mace blessed by the gods. For clergy, nothing is more reassuring than holding it. Facing the Kin of Darkness, it senses their evil, grows angry and heats up. At times it gets hot enough to burn, yet clergy grip it gladly, saying, "I can feel the gods' love."
According to the Goblins, a being of great power once used this ladle to guide the people of the land. It is plain, yet holding it is said to fill you with a warm, somehow nostalgic feeling.

A weapon easy to make and easy to use. It lacks power and reach, but it is cheap and handy when you just want something in hand for now. Then again, it feels like you could make one yourself in the dungeon if it came to that.

A club made of iron, not wood. So vicious it makes the Wood Club look like a toy. A hit from this is far worse than "ouch": it strikes hard enough that a blow to the head might well cave in the skull.

A club made solely to beat people to death. The grudges of all it has killed cling to it along with their blood. Anyone it strikes either thrashes about wildly, as if fleeing the agony, or doubles over in mute torment.

A beautiful club of clear crystal with a finely decorated grip. The crystal holds such strong magic that it normally can't be touched. It seems you strike with the crystal, but you really strike with the magic barrier around it, so it never breaks however hard you swing.

A ranged weapon used by all sorts of people. Poor at rapid fire, but in skilled hands it easily kills foes before they get close. By nature, though, it leaves you defenseless, with no way to attack, once a foe gets inside your guard, so carry a Dagger or the like for self-defense.

As the name says, a bow with far greater range than the Bow. Its range and power can strike down a target so far off it looks like a speck. Only real experts can do that, though: on top of aiming, drawing a Longbow takes great strength, and the training is hard.

A cursed bow of warped wood. A twisted bow makes a twisted shot. Aiming at the enemy and hitting an ally in the rear is a common occurrence. Some daredevils use the twist to land telling shots, but it's hardly worth going that far.

A bow from a far eastern land, holding power to dispel darkness. It glows when it senses darkness, guiding its demon-slaying arrows. Great on the attack, but a bit awkward when it flashes as you try to flee or hide. Then again, with this bow you'll rarely need to run.

A bow fixed to a gauntlet for better accuracy and control, letting you hit targets precisely even on the run. But it leaves you even more vulnerable once foes close in, so you must keep running and shoot from a distance. Maybe that hassle is the real curse.

The bow said to have been favored by Polyte the Bow Saint. Its emerald-green body was said to call the wind of victory to the battlefield, rousing every ally fighting there. It is also known for the emerald-green sparks that scatter the instant an arrow flies.

A bow said to have been made by a sorcerer who lives underground. No arrows needed: draw the string at the sky, and sharp diamond crystals appear overhead and rain down. It's dangerous, so always warn your allies before you shoot.

They say spirits sometimes borrow the strength of a trusted Ranger to protect the nature they love. This bow is the weapon they hand over then. Its power is superb, but it is the one bow that can never be drawn against a spirit.
A cowhide whip that makes a fine crack. They say a lashing does great mental damage on top of the pain.
A whip made not of cowhide but of iron. Where an ordinary whip lashes the body, the Iron Whip also strips away flesh and fighting spirit alike.
A whip that silences whoever it lashes. Is it the whip's doing, or are they cowed by its wielder...? Either way, it's a blow you'd rather not take.
A bright red whip like a great serpent's tongue. It was named for how its lashing looks just like a great serpent striking. True to its name, it also inflicts deadly poison.

Stronger, more elegant. A steel whip evolved further from the Iron Whip. Years of research let it bend just like a normal whip despite being metal. Some adventurers have become different people after getting one. No surprise there.

Said to be the whip of the Hell Master, jailer of hell. Its backward barbs catch skin and flesh as it is pulled free, causing agony. The pain is horrible to imagine; some demons cower at the mere sight. A dream weapon every whip user longs to own.
A simple wooden staff, standard gear for spellcasting classes. Just as it looks, don't expect much from it as a weapon. Maybe it's good for leaning on when you walk?

A small, light staff made just for Fairies. Light, yet carved from sturdy wood, so its attack and durability barely differ from an ordinary staff. A miniature of the ordinary staff, you might call it.

The main weapon of the Kannagi, said to be the eastern version of the Priest. Just an odd stick with strange paper strips at the tip, yet it is especially powerful against spirits and undead monsters.

So battered you could mistake it for a mere branch, it has lost its original form. Being all wood, a staff needs daily care, and neglected it rots easily, like this. Once rotted, nothing will ever restore it, so return it to nature.

A rod rich with a fire spirit's power, granting its holder fire's protection. Besides boosting fire power, it lets even those without magic power cast fire magic by swinging it. Its magic never runs out however much it is used, so it's handy even as a backup.

Even as a staff, it still holds the breath of life, and that vitality greatly protects its user. As its life fades, its green leaves turn brown and wither until it is just a staff. To prevent this: daily care, watering, and playing it music or talking to it.
A holy rod blessed by the gods. It grants its holder the courage of light and the power to repel evil forces. It is also highly valued as an antique.
A staff that points to the next one to die. The Reaper is said to go about reaping the souls of those this staff marks. A staff of darkness that curses its owner, too.

Imbued with spirit power, it shields its holder from every kind of elemental attack. It lends aid in attack too, yet the Elemental Wand itself dislikes strife. Legend says that if used only for fighting, it will one day lose the spirits' blessing.
A staff meant for spellcasters versed in every spell. Any half-baked mage who takes it up is said to be driven mad by its magic. Wielding great power, it seems, takes matching power.

Hand wraps may look like mere bandages on the fists, but there is a reason. One is to cushion punches and protect the fists; the other is to brace them against sprains. Unlike Fighters with swords, a Gladiator's weapons are their own fists, a treasure beyond price.

People tend to think a boomerang mows down foes, then circles back to your hand. But a real one lacks the mass to keep its course after hitting, and simply drops when it hits something. If by some fluke it does come back, run. It's dangerous.

The kunai is a weapon for assassination: easy to carry, easy to hide, and highly lethal. Throwing one so it sticks in a target is very hard and takes real skill. Once you can throw it and hit, it truly becomes an all-purpose weapon.

The torture device long known as the 'Iron Maiden,' made into a weapon. Besides impaling those shut inside on its spikes, it opens and shuts freely and is lighter and more mobile. Still bulky and of limited use, it is hard to handle, and few can wield it.

No ordinary hawk's: the talon of Balteris, the monster bird of the mountains. Its tip holds poison, rubbed in as it cuts, that causes confusion and hallucinations and robs the foe of all sense of distance. A great edge for Gladiators, who have no reach.

A Mage's Crystal has no power alone, but gains limitless power from its holder's magic and can be moved by magic without being held. If an enemy mage wields one freely, beware: in earnest, they can whip that darting crystal right in front of your face in an instant.

Knuckles of a legendary ore said to sleep deep in the earth. They awaken the power sleeping deep in a Gladiator's body, unleashing true strength. Blades on the fists add punching power, and can also catch an enemy's sword and the like.

The Ninja's basic yet strongest weapon. Unlike the kunai, it is mainly thrown; spinning steadies its flight. Kunai are hard to hit with, but shuriken hit easily, so the two are used together. Loosed near-silently from darkness, they sow deep fear in foes.
A fairy tale in which Notis, a prince mocked for his long nose, rescues a princess kidnapped by the Demon Lord. Popular with children, it is a favorite first book for new parents to buy their child.

A book of pictures and write-ups of eastern monsters, with legends and tales about them. Inside, it is packed with oni, tengu, kappa and other unique monsters. Indeed, unlike monsters here, they are insidious and very creepy. Trust the East: it's not just the classes that are odd.

A book applying spell theory to economics, a revolutionary idea in its day. Its economics are actually little use. Frankly, they're nonsense. But the spell theory used to explain them is so detailed that it is hugely popular as a spellbook rather than an economics text.

This tale tells of a boy raised as a girl and a girl raised as a boy. 'Torikaebaya' is said to be old Eastern for 'I wish I could swap such-and-such.' In the tale, it's the two children's sexes, but I don't think you can just swap those because you want to. A cultural difference, perhaps?

A book of all kinds of hush-hush knowledge. Its content is... well... indecent. But since it varies by race and customs differ by culture, it is at times studied quite seriously. Once, a rumor that releasing SP lets you reach Master Level sold it out continent-wide.

A detailed history of this continent. Scholars drew on every surviving record and talked to people who lived in those times to revive the history very accurately. Now and then, why not look back at the history of those who came before?

Those without the right see nothing in this book. But those who have it are said to see a mysterious string of letters, which differs for each reader and changes over time. Well, care to try it yourself?

An encyclopedia of everything in the world. A very heavy, thick book whose contents are no joke. Constantly updated by the continent's Central Library, it keeps growing; reading it all alone is said to be impossible. Even its editors know only their own sections.
A shield made for deflecting and parrying attacks. It is a bit too weak to rely on for blocking blows head-on, so use it to shut down enemy attacks as early as you can.

A medium shield, bigger and heavier than a Buckler. It blocks attacks more easily, but held close to the body it creates a large blind spot. Being heavier, it can't make some moves a Buckler can, so adjust how you use it.

Unlike the Buckler and such, which suit a range of classes, it is made for warrior classes, and built sturdily. Naturally it is heavy and needs real strength to handle, but the sense of security it gives once equipped is great.
A shield that looks cursed through and through. The picture on it is said to depict the sun. It does sort of look like one... But nothing can be done about the sheer menace oozing from it.

Made of beast bone alone, with no iron at all. Lacking iron or other usual shield materials, it is very light and easy to handle. Nor is it brittle just because it is bone: it is far harder and tougher than any run-of-the-mill iron shield.

A Knight Shield a rank above, with care put into its materials and ornament alike. It uses red and gold for splendor, with a lion ornament at its center as a symbol of strength. Knights who gain a Knight Shield +1 are said to swell with new pride and duty.

Like the rest of the Innocent series, a shield only those who mastered one path without ever straying may wear. It is simple, but holding it surely feeds the confidence that you have mastered your path.
A shield painted with a strange eye pattern. It hardly looks holy, but you do sense some such power. Then again, maybe the foes you fight and the beings this shield hates just happen to be the same?

This shield holds holy power and is favored by those who serve the gods, such as Valkyries. Made of light iron, it is light and easy to handle. Light iron is said to break easily, but perhaps thanks to divine blessing, this shield is far from fragile. If your Priest fights up front, give them one.

Modeled on a demon's wing: light, hard, easy to use and very effective. But only those of Evil alignment can use it. In the hands of someone with a conscience, it loses its power at once and is no better than a scrap of iron plate.

A shield polished like a mirror. Its surface is said never to scratch, however heavy the blow. This mirror is also said to show things' true forms; since no lie can be told before it, it was named the Truth Shield.

Some demons have mighty wings that ordinary swords cannot beat. The Demon Wing is a shield crafted from such a dead demon's wings. Some say people were 'eaten' by it and became demons. Handle it with great care. It is of the Kin of Darkness, after all.
A sturdy shield of mithril, said to repel any attack to protect its owner. It is fine armor, but some adventurers seek it solely to sell to nobles wanting prestige.

A shield of dragon scales fitted together. Making one means slaying a mighty dragon, so it counts as a rarity. Scale patterns differ with each dragon, so it is prized as art and has many collectors. Given its value, shoddy fakes of dragon scale circulate, too.

A miraculous shield said to be born when the light of truth reaches the darkness of myth. You perceived the lost divine power, and this shield will protect you all your life. Use it in a crisis, and it will call down its power of old for you.

The head is the most dangerous place for people or monsters to be hit. As the name says, this helm is leather: worse than iron headgear, but many classes can wear it. Made of many layers of hide, it gets stuffy in hot places or in summer.

Besides iron ones, they say some were of hide or of washi paper hardened with lacquer, but perhaps since the craft was lost, only iron ones exist now. It is quite heavy, yet its defense does not match its weight, so its faults stand out.

A helm shaped like an upturned iron bucket. It covers the front down to about the nose and the back down to the nape, a reassuring design for defense. But it badly limits vision, so as a remedy, a horizontal slit is cut at eye level.
A distinctive helm whose face juts out like a bird's beak. Odd as it looks, the shape works well to deflect blows from the front. The face part also moves, and can be flipped up when not needed.

A helm made from a demon's skull, giving off a baleful aura. It seems the demon was powerful in life, and strong demonic power remains in the skull even after death. Clergy who carelessly touch it are said to lose their sanity.

A helm shaped to cover the whole face, said to be modeled on the sallet and the Bascinet. Its name comes from the back of the helm resembling a flower. Since it covers the whole head, it gives the head quite high defense.

Paired with the Evil Shield and the like. Armor is mostly designed and made in sets from head to toe, and the Evil series is no exception. Wear this blood-dyed helm into battle, and foes will see you as a demon drenched head to toe in your enemies' blood.

A helm that now guards the back of the head and neck, which the Ashigaru Helm could not. Its sides bend back by the face, a technique called fukigaeshi. In the East, mid-rank samurai all wear one; they rank about like company captains here.

A helm aiming for total defense by covering the whole face. It does raise defense, but you can't communicate by expression, which can breed distrust; take care, more so if you are quiet. When forming a new party, it's only polite to take it off now and then to smile.

A mask worn at masquerade balls and the like, to hide one's status and enjoy a night of glamour. But some wear it with other feelings. What heart dwells in this cursed mask? Only one who wears it could know.

A ring woven of young laurel twigs with leaves is a laurel wreath. Laurel has long been known as a sacred tree, and a ring is thought to circulate and amplify its power. That power is so strong it defends far better than any mere crown of leaves.

A helm modeled on a dragon's head. It is good armor, and it also lets even those not of dragon kin use breath attacks. How it inherited the dragon's power, and how it is made, remains shrouded in mystery.

A princess's headband that every woman dreams of. Its intricate ornament turns its surroundings silver in even faint light. Women are curious things: with one tiara, the air about them turns crystal clear. Maybe that is the Silver Tiara's real magic.

A golden helm with a pair of horn-like metal ornaments at the sides of the brow. The rest is mostly gold, too, making it very lavish. Its wearers are captains and lords; the color is said to cry "A lord stands here!", rousing allies and daunting foes.

Made to cover the entire head, using rare mithril generously. Made of iron, it would weigh so much it would badly restrict movement, but mithril made it lighter and harder. The drawback, as you'd expect, is how rare mithril is.
A hat so fluffy you'll want to snuggle it on sight. It is warm, and more cold-weather gear than armor. It is hard to wash, though, so try not to get it dirty, or wash it gently.
A hat of black-lacquered paper, made with a unique Eastern technique to be strong enough for combat. Said to be part of the Kannagi's formal attire, it is apparently quite prestigious.

A cotton handkerchief, tie-dyed or printed in calico patterns, is called a bandana when tied around the head. They come in many patterns and colors, so every bandana has its own character. Being a handkerchief at heart, it has many uses beyond being worn, such as wiping sweat or stanching blood.

A hat torn in fierce combat. Few garments come through battles full of flying swords, arrows and spells unscathed. Conversely, if you see an adventurer wearing gear like this without a speck of dirt on it, you should assume they are highly skilled.

A strange hat that has sprouted wings. A miracle of the gods, or a devil's prank? Wear it and you feel you could fly, but only the hat would fly away. The wings are linked to the wearer's mood and move in funny ways: twitching when happy, flapping when flustered, folding shut when sulking.

A wig is normally an adornment for the head. What situation could call for wearing a wig with no hair? A truly baffling item. Yet the most baffling thing of all must be the fact that monsters drop these. Hair Remover! Hair Remember!

Naturally, some adventurers are women. So as not to forget she is a woman before she is an adventurer, she adorns herself with a steel hairband. A little touch of style: will that special someone like it? Giving your all in love and adventure! Let's go, girls!

A hat made for Mages. It completely nullifies silence spells. Nothing can stop the chanting of a caster wearing it; foes can only flee from the spells unleashed. But Mages, keep one thing in mind: magic power is not infinite. Get carried away and you may get burned.

This hood senses its wearer's tastes and endlessly tells them jokes funny enough to make them die laughing. So hilarious are they that the wearer forgets all knowledge. Yet knowledge alone would be fine. Wear this hood in public, and your authority and trust will also be socially LOST.

A Bandana Soul fires you up more than a bandana. It began when a Gladiator in a bandana cried, "This bandana has no soul! I need one with soul in it! First, how it's tied!" and tied it their own way. A bandana's soul: Bandana Soul. Obvious, really, yet it's a hit with Gladiators and Rangers.

A hat knitted from magic thread to raise magic power. Wearing it is sure to amplify a Mage's power. The greater the wearer's power to begin with, the stronger the boost, so a decent caster becomes a strong one, and a strong caster becomes an unstoppable one.

Armor of iron that covers the whole body. Being iron, it gives high defense, but it is very heavy in exchange. For front-liners, it is the gear that lets them cover themselves head to toe and breathe easy for the time being.

Full-body armor made for knights, designed with mounted combat in mind. Knights in national service, except captains, are issued this armor. Its basic performance differs little from Plate Mail, but it is somewhat easier to move in.

For those who fight on the front line in full armor, armor is a consumable. However well they dodge, no one can avoid every attack, and those attacks rarely leave just a scratch. Yet to the wearer, such armor may be a mark of pride. Provided, of course, the wearer is still alive.
Raw meat of the giant creature Airy Vider. The meat is so huge that to bring it back, you must either travel by magic or carry it on your back, roped to your body.

Plate Mail made lighter by shaving off needless parts while keeping the same material. It was made with input from those who actually wore Plate Mail on the front line, so it is well liked in the field. The word is: rather than buy Plate Mail, stretch your budget a little and buy Plate Mail +1.

Neither good nor evil. Neither ally nor foe. Only such a one, seeking to stop a pointless fight between both sides, may wear this armor. The Neutral alignment is generally thought hard to grasp. That shows how many live by cozy collusion. Neutral adventurers, be noble.

Armor with magic-defense spells cast over its whole surface. They are little more than a charm, but having them or not makes a world of difference. Fighters, poor in magic defense, favor it. It is one of the armors spellcasters find most troublesome.

Bright red armor, as if dyed all over in blood. Foes on the battlefield are said to have feared its wearers, taking them for demons. Nor was that wholly a mistake: all who wear it fight cruelly, and when the battle ends, blood drips from every inch of the armor.

Gleaming armor made of crystal. Being see-through, it is often assumed to be light, but it is a solid lump of stone and quite heavy. Unlike other armor, you also have to watch what you wear underneath it.

Armor said to last a lifetime once you have it. However, given the high price of mithril and its beauty, Mithril Plate was traded mainly for display. Even when used on the battlefield, it is rarely seen on the front line.
Armor blessed by the gods, which only those of high standing may wear. Only Lords can equip it, but if you obtain it, its wearer will become an even more dependable guardian of the party.

Gear designed to protect the wearer's chest. Unlike full armor it covers only the torso, so it is easy to move in and favored by swift warriors who live by hit-and-run. Defense or mobility? On that, opinions are divided among wearers.

Armor worn by low-ranking samurai in the eastern land. Its defense is modest, but it is so versatile it is easy to mass-produce. That made it cheap to equip a whole unit, and it was prized for giving a unit a uniform look and sense of unity.

A fallen samurai is an eastern samurai who survived a war on the losing side and fled. Such a fugitive's armor is called Fallen Samurai Armor. Its wearer was attacked while fleeing, so its back bristles with enemy arrows. They ran for their lives, with no time to pull them from armor or body.

A breastplate for Rangers, with no shoulder strap on the right side to make drawing a bow easier. Besides guarding the chest, it also serves as a guard to keep the bowstring from injuring the wearer's chest.

Armor that spoiled young nobles wore to the battlefield on a lark, which at some point began circulating among the public. It is pretty enough that some want to wear it, but it is like parading your wealth, so be ready to be attacked now and then.
Armor said to have been worn by swordsmen of the eastern land while guarding the coast. It is far more decent than Ashigaru Armor. Perhaps because it puts practicality first, it is extremely plain.

A breastplate made of white silver. It shines beautifully, but tarnishes quickly if neglected. If you get splashed with blood, wipe it off fast. Some alchemists take on polishing jobs for armor of this kind.

An ice breastplate wreathed in cold. Its chill lets it lessen fire attacks a little. But its true worth lies in special defense. Perhaps it chills the heart, too, for it fully nullifies several special attacks. A lasting favorite of mid- to high-level adventurers.

Armor made to offer victory to the goddess. Legend says battle maidens wore such offered armor into war. Following that legend, it is still made today for Valkyries. Wearing it, they gain the pride and strength of the battle maidens who guarded the goddess.

This kuroito odoshi is said to be made in a special style of the eastern land. That style never reached this continent, so the only ones here were brought over from the East somehow. With beauty as well as defense, this armor is truly a mystery of the East.

Chain mail's most notable trait is that, unlike other armor, it is very flexible. It barely restricts movement. Also, worn at all times outside battle, it protects you from sudden raids and assassins. It may be the armor you can keep closest at hand.

Armor made of many overlapping cut iron plates. It combines iron's high defense with a chain-mail-like flexibility that fits the body. But it is hard to maintain; slip up and the iron joints soon rust, leaving it useless. So some people never maintain it at all and just treat it as disposable.

Chain mail made with elven magic arts. On top of normal chain mail performance, it resists magic, making it an all-round design. But as it is made with magic arts known only to elves, humans cannot wear it.

Chain mail with the power of fire woven into its links. Wearing it protects you from cold. Also, casting fire spells creates a synergy that deals more damage than usual. Its powers are the exact opposite of Ice Chain Mail's; the two are a matched pair.

Chain mail with the power of ice woven into its links. Wearing it protects you from fire. Also, casting ice spells creates a synergy that deals more damage than usual. Its powers are the exact opposite of Flame Chain Mail's; the two are a matched pair.

Why does adding a face covering to chain mail make it look so eerie? In fact, chain mail of this shape was used to transport prisoners and criminals. It was not meant to guard against foes outside, but to keep the threat inside from getting out.

Chain mail blessed by a god and imbued with holy power. The blessing guards the wearer from dark magic and amplifies holy magic. Being chain mail, it can be worn under a habit without anyone noticing. Partly for that reason, it is the gear clergy favor most.

Chain mail holding the powers of fire and ice at once. As chain mail, its defense is not absolute, but its special effect gives high resistance to fire and ice spells and amplifies both. Fire and ice rarely coexist; this chain mail truly deserves to be called a miracle.
Unlike iron armor, which is picky about classes, leather armor can be worn by a great many classes. Everyone wears it at least once.

Even animal hide becomes fairly sturdy armor if you take the trouble to boil it in wax and harden it. It is a bit heavier, but acceptably so given its strength. However, the extra work raises the price too, so it is a judgment call.
Leather armor rotted to tatters. What became of the one who wore it? Did they escape safely, or were they left to lie in the dungeon along with this armor?

Leather armor set with gems. At first glance, setting gems into it seems utterly pointless. But these gems hold a faint trace of spirit power, and they are set into the leather in hopes of that power.

Made from parts of a dragon that could never be used for proper armor, such as the soft parts of its scales. Even so, it is still dragon, so it has defense to match. Every part of a dragon is precious, so all of it is used and nothing goes to waste.

Robes are thought of as giving only token protection. But that is a mistake. Some are woven of thread soaked in holy water to raise holy defense, or reinforced with magic thread or monster hair. Well, this robe is just a robe.

Clothes made for Fairies only. They are far too small for anyone else to wear. Small as they are, they have real defense and durability. For a Fairy, already nimble, just wearing these should be quite effective.

Black garb favored by assassins of the eastern land, so they can melt into the dark and kill their target unnoticed. Besides camouflage, it is designed for ease of movement; you could call it gear made for assassins. If you hear even a faint sound from empty darkness, be on your guard.
A robe worn to tatters and full of holes. But it is only natural for a robe to end up in tatters. It is just cloth, after all; asking a robe for durability and defense is simply unfair.
A robe given some toughness. Due to the kind of material used, it turned green all over. It is sturdier than a plain robe, but that is all it is.

Originally a training uniform called a dogi, from the eastern land. Those like Gladiators, whose own fists are their deadliest weapon, find it very comfortable, so it is now made for Gladiators. It is easy to move in, absorbs sweat well, and makes special moves easy to pull off.

Whether or not anyone actually cried "The Green Robe won't do!", here is a robe with even more toughness. Due to the material, this time it turned blue. Many mistakenly imagine it has something to do with ice spells, but it does not, at all.

Formal attire of the Kannagi, a sort of eastern Priest. Its sheer silken overgarment and faintly crimson cherry blossom embroidery are lovely. Some adventurers are said to become Kannagi out of longing for this outfit. And it's not only lovely: it also protects, making it a fine pick as armor too.
A robe adorned with crests to raise magic resistance. The boost may be slight, but if it improves your odds of coming through unscathed, so much the better.
Made of extremely light material, it sways in breezes too faint to feel, hence the name. Since it is always wrapped in a fresh breeze, it can blow away mild drowsiness.

A bright red robe that reduces fire damage. Common low-level fire spells become mere trifles. Its brilliant crimson glow makes you the center of attention just by walking. Stride through town with its hem flaring, and everyone will turn to look.

A robe holding the power of lightning. It is said to be woven from thread blessed by Zilphe. It has very high resistance to lightning magic; ordinary lightning attacks won't hurt you no matter how many you take.

A robe of black and milky white in lovely contrast, like the midnight moon. Light and dark dwell together in it, giving it both Holy and Dark attributes. Its thin, light cloth looks nearly useless, but moonlike light and black mist envelop the wearer, giving very high defense.

The finest robe, which only Bishops may wear. Thanks to protective spells woven into it, light as it is, it gives better evasion than common armor. A Bishop who can wear this robe has truly come into their own.

Gauntlets made of leather. The soft leather keeps them light and the fingers nimble, so you can react instantly to all kinds of situations. In exchange, their defense is meager; they feel close to ordinary gloves.

Gloves for Fairies only. They are so tiny that ordinary people cannot possibly wear them. Small as they are, they are very finely made. Only fairy artisans make this possible; human or elven fingers could never make them.

Hand guards developed in the eastern land. The plated back can parry powerful slashes, but that takes a great deal of training. The fingers are said to be left free of iron to make holding a katana or drawing a bow easier.

Gauntlets made of iron. They are segmented like bellows to protect the whole hand and fingers while allowing some freedom. You can't spread your hand wide, but you can grip a sword with no trouble at all.
Gauntlets slashed to ribbons. They have taken so many blows that they can no longer serve as armor. Perhaps out of the former owner's bitter regret, equipping them will curse you.
Gloves with a protective spell placed on the back of the hand. Don't expect much defense, but they raise resistance to spells. Note that they do not raise the power of your spells.

Lovely rose-adorned gauntlets only women who fight may wear. For whom does a lone rose blooming on the battlefield swing her sword? By this continent's custom, you don't get Rose Gauntlets yourself; they should be a gift from someone close to your heart. If you get some, give them to that someone!
Gauntlets made of steel. Crafted with the finger joints in mind, they let you grip a sword as naturally as with bare hands. Their defense is high as well, which makes them popular.

Gloves of bobbin lace. They are costly, as an artisan must spend vast amounts of time making them. But they are worth the price; the lace is superb. The thread is soaked in holy water at a temple, so they hold holy power.
Gauntlets in the shape of a mantis. Insect monsters will flee at the mere sight of them. But insects are not the only ones who fear mantises. You understand, don't you?

Gloves modeled on the hands of Death. The bones on the back are a demon's hand bones. Wear these with a black robe and a great scythe, and you'll look every bit the Reaper. Just don't get carried away and summon the real thing.

Gauntlets made of mithril, said to be so light you forget you have them on. Their defense is high too; they can take anything from sword slashes to a giant monster's claws. They need less mithril than shields or armor, so many have been made.

Made of divinely blessed metal and a large bloodstone. Bloodstones have many uses, such as adorning a temple's holy statues, so one this large is a rare luxury. Treat them carelessly and lose them, and you'll make an enemy of every priest on the continent.

Buskins are half-boots with thick cork soles. Being cork, they have almost no durability; it is no different from walking barefoot. They are also very light: again, no different from walking barefoot. In other words, they are a matter of appearances.
Slippers woven from straw, common in the eastern land. Being straw, they are extremely light. Samurai are especially fond of them and rarely want to wear anything else on their feet.

Boots come in many kinds. Colors and shapes, of course, but materials also vary widely. Of all those boots, these were made for tramping around battlefields and dungeons. Note that, as with all boots, they get sweaty, so... frankly, they stink.
Boots made for roaming forests and streams. They are full of touches that hide your presence from small animals and the like. Sneak up on any animal in these, and it will take a fatal blow.

Boots made of iron. Being iron through and through, they make flexing the ankles and other joints very hard. Add the weight of armor and helm and it gets very heavy, so first practice walking in just the boots, without armor or the like.

Lustrous, beautiful dancing shoes. They bear a former owner's sin and curse: whoever wears them will dance until they die. To take them off, you may have to sacrifice your feet. Will the day ever come when the sin is forgiven...?
Boots made of steel. Making the most of steel's properties, they are well balanced and easy to walk in. Any mid-level adventurer should make a point of getting a pair.
Shoes made by dwarven craftsmen. Made of sturdy material, they give firm footing even on somewhat rough ground. Non-dwarves can equip them too.

Boots holding fire magic. They are fine armor, and they also amplify fire power and reduce ice damage. Despite the name Fire Boots, they won't burn your feet when you put them on, so equip them without worry.
Beautiful shoes made of silver. In good condition, their gleam in the sun can be seen from quite far away. Made with almost no seams, they won't let water in from below, even when you wade in.

Sandals with a dainty pair of little wings. Holy power dwells in this armor, and a protective force is at work. Talk to them and the wings seem to flutter in reply... or is that just your imagination?

Platinum slippers. Like gold, platinum resists acid. They are so tough and durable that a pair, once found, may be handed down for generations in an adventurer's family. Dig through your closet and you may find Grandpa's or Grandma's Platinum Slippers. Maybe their platinum dentures too.
Pitch-black boots that melt into the darkness. Assassins favor them, so most who own them never die a decent death.
Shoes made of a mysterious glass. You can wear them normally, and they won't break even if you run. Rumor has it that sometimes only one is ever found.

Shoes wrapped in a white radiance. Their holy power reaches even your footsteps; it's said a mere stamp drives off lesser spirits. Priests in this world can serve in the front or back row, but if you put one up front, do give them these.

A cloak worn by many adventurers on their first outing. Don't expect much defense; it serves more to keep out the cold. To keep it affordable even for novices, it has no decoration at all and is priced as low as possible.
A belt martial artists wear as proof of their own training. If your opponent is wearing one, you'd do well to be on your guard.

A grubby cloak with clasps and buttons coming loose. Your time is finite. Waste it aimlessly and your cloak, too, will soon look like this. And yet the eyes of the fallen have not lost themselves. Why might that be?
A cloak dyed a refreshing blue. It has no special power, but its looks make it surprisingly popular. Some seasoned adventurers even wear this weak cloak on purpose, as a matter of taste.

A cloak that blesses those who find the path they must follow. Its defense is modest, but its spell resistance is strong. Even high-level adventurers are said to find it hard to part with. Some who lose the right to wear it can't bear to toss the cloak that saw them through their youth.

A mantle styled on the new moon. A new-moon night, out of light's reach, is called the 'Holy Darkness,' Yaha, when the Kin of Darkness are said to be weakest. Yes, darkness is not always evil. It is a holy chaos that births the power to live, a cradle of the heart that soothes the soul.

An apron only fully trained servants may wear. The dirtier it gets, the more its wearer is said to have served their master. Each master, and each servant, needs different work done, so the 'Master Apron' comes in many forms.
A cloak with a griffon's wings worked into it. The power of the noble magical beast is said to grant its wearer a courage that flinches before nothing.
Great wings of jet black beat only in dreams. Wrap yourself in this mantle and darkness is your ally. Cast off the base light, and welcome to the farthest reaches of the heart.
A mirage is an illusion. This cloak acts on the space around you, making your image appear many times over. Sluggish foes will hardly ever land a hit.

A tail yanked off a Tonafel. It protects its owner from sleep. It also serves as emergency rations: soak it in hot water and it will fill your belly a bit. But it is only emergency food; try as you might, it will never taste good.

"Every adventurer ought to wear this cloth as underwear," say those from the East, but it's rather embarrassing. If you don't mind, wearing one to learn another culture could be fun. Its unique look and feel win some people over.
The bat in the center is iron, but the belt around it is genuine bat leather. Somehow the belt gives off faint ultrasonic waves that protect its owner from confusion.
This is what a fundoshi becomes when worn and its special power is unleashed. Depending on who owned it before, it may come with added value.
A rune born in the process of making Magic Puppets. By promoting self-repair, it covers the weakness of Magic Puppets, which have no metabolism.

A belt made of bones of many races, human and elf skulls among them. It is said to be made by demons, for demons. The grudges of those killed for its materials dwell in it. It seems a cruel item, but in truth the demons merely copied what we do.

Only one person in the world may wear this belt: proof of the mightiest Gladiator. Wear it and you'll be fired up even more. In name there is only one, but you may pick up several on your travels. Yet do not seek value in the belt. Grow strong, so the belt you wear gains value.
Magic paper in everyday use by Kannagi. How it is made is unknown, but it gives off a power to drive off evil, especially strong against wicked beings and beings of darkness.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of fire. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a Mage, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of ice. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a Mage, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of lightning. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a Mage, equip at least the next rank up.

A large flower that blooms deep in the forest, rather eerie-looking for a flower. Yet it has long been an offering to the gods and, despite its looks, is highly prized. Rolfan pollen blocks other pollens and scents, which is said to be one reason it became an offering.
An ember guarded by fire spirits; to obtain it, you must first win the spirits over. Elves can reportedly use this ember to craft special armor with high magic defense, a craft known only to elves.

The gem on a Carbuncle's brow. Beautiful and resistant to all sorts of magic, it was once so popular that Carbuncles were overhunted, nearly to extinction. Things have calmed down now, but they still fiercely menace any human who approaches.

Down of the Phoenix, famed as immortal. It strongly boosts and resists fire magic, but you must defeat a Phoenix to get it, so it's very rare. Beyond magic, it may stuff the pillows and quilts of the very rich: light and wonderfully warm, far beyond any common down quilt.

This egg is a delicacy, on almost everyone's list of 'foods to try before I die.' To get one, just take an egg from an Emperor Bird's nest. But a parent guarding its young fights beyond its strength, so don't take it lightly.
A wooden box for keeping medicine. Its design came from a land in the East; it is built to stay dry at all times so the medicine inside won't spoil.

The one scale under a dragon's jaw that grows the wrong way is called the 'reverse scale.' Touch it and the dragon flies into a rage and never forgives whoever did. Dragonewts, too, keep a trace of it. It varies by person, but touching it does make them openly annoyed.
A misanga dyed in a savage rabbit's blood. A normal misanga snaps when your wish comes true, but this one grants no wishes and never snaps. Instead, it severs your foe's head from its body.

God, demon, soul, matter. A talisman held by a Kannagi who served, and was loved by, the unknowable power ruling all creation. Ordinary folk can touch it unharmed, but any lowly spirit around would be blown away just by coming near.
A small wooden box engraved with an emblem meaning 'ruler of the world.' Hold it aloft and your foes will tremble in awe and bow down.
A ring set with a pearl. Its pearl is special: a magic-charged pearl said to be a mermaid's gift. Perhaps for that reason, it gives a slight resistance to poison.

A jade ring famed for having no seam, a showcase of craftsmanship. With no seam, the gem's magic circulates almost forever, multiplying its power two- and threefold. Elves named this the 'Bole Effect,' and many rings use it. As armor, it wards off minor ailments.
A ring made of cockatrice bone. Wearing it grants resistance to petrification. In other words, equip it and you can go cockatrice hunting again.
At a glance, an unremarkable wooden ring. Since no one can tell them apart, plain wooden rings sometimes circulate as Sacred Wood Rings. It protects against paralysis.

A ring whose diamond's pure brilliance is said to repel wicked thoughts. It wards off silence, a boon for Mages. Now and then one turns up with a diamond tinted red, blue, green or another lovely color. These are rare and sell high, but their magic is weaker.
A ring rusted all over, from who knows what era. Nothing remains of its original form.
A ring only Fairies are permitted to wear. It is so tiny that even finding one is hard. Small as it is, it bears decoration, and some fetch very high prices.

A ring set with a gem bearing a pattern like a cat's eye. 'Cat's eye' names a pattern; some stones take it readily, but there is no actual stone called cat's eye. Some Cat's Eye Rings are said to be ultra-rare: gems already magical that went even more cat.

A ring that slowly restores its wearer's health. Words of thanks to the gods are carved on it; treated with heart, it stands in for a Priest's healing spells. Alchemy can do the same, but it uses the laws of the earth; it does not ask the gods for a miracle as Priests do.
A ring adorned with a skull. When worn, the skull's eyes begin to glow red. They are said to glow because it is drawing in the wearer's life force.
A ring that gives form to a vow to stay friends forever. This token of friendship across races will show its power in the hands of Mages and Summoners.
An ankh that governs strength. Unleash its hidden power and still greater strength will fill your body.
An ankh that governs intellect. Unleash its hidden power and still more intellect will enrich your mind.
An ankh that governs piety. Unleash its hidden power, and by the gods' guidance the path you must walk will come into view.
An ankh that governs vitality. Unleash its hidden power and your body will know no fatigue.
An ankh that governs agility. Unleash its hidden power and you will be able to move faster than the eye can see.
An ankh that governs luck. Unleash its hidden power and you will gain luck second to none.

An ointment that has gone along on adventures since long ago, made by blending various herbs in fixed proportions. Every item shop stocks it, and it's reasonably priced. An essential for novice adventurers.
Unlike Salve, this medicine is taken by mouth. It is colorless and clear, with a refreshing sweet-tart taste reminiscent of citrus.

Sprinkle this on a sleeper, and however deep the sleep, they wake in an instant. It truly wakes anyone, even rousing people who've been up for nights on end, so it once became a health issue. Now it's regulated in many places: adventurers buy it freely, others only once their purpose is checked.

A little antidote herb steeped in water. The herb is addictive: swallowed as-is, it cures poison but brings on 'antidote herb addiction.' People used to hold it in the mouth a while, then spit it out, but young adventurers don't know that trick, so it became a bottled drink.

Herbs that neutralize toxins, steeped in water. The compound is water-soluble. Eaten as-is, they work once digested, but when monsters attack there's no time for that. So adventurers wisely began steeping them beforehand to extract it, and in time the idea became a product.

A candy that soothes the throat. Suck one and your voice comes right back. It works wonders and tastes great, so you'll keep reaching for one when your mouth is bored. Watch out: they're often gone just when you need them! If you can't resist, let another adventurer carry them.

An herb that calms the confused. Just tear off a leaf and let them smell it; the scent will restore their composure. But beware: let them sniff every leaf at once, and they'll go past calm into apathy.
It cures charm. It's a genuine medicinal crystal, but who on earth gave it this name? Middle-aged adventurers find it rather embarrassing to buy.

Water that undoes petrification. It starts as an acid, which alchemy turns into a cure for stone flesh. The body fizzes back to normal, which those who've tried it say feels rather good. Still, asking a mage for a petrify spell plus Stonemelt Water is outright mage harassment. Don't.
A mysterious elixir that can call a soul back into its body. Hold it and you'll find it as warm as skin. Pour it into a dead person's mouth and, unless their soul is lost, they will awaken.

A cure-all for not just headaches but nearly every minor ailment. It was made for townsfolk, so adventurers only lately learned of its effect. The market sets its price so existing drugs' prices won't crash: dear for adventurers who go out and dive into trouble, cheap for townsfolk.
A scroll holding a sleep spell. Use it to grant your foes a peaceful sleep. It is sometimes used as a cure for insomnia, too.
A scroll holding a light spell. Use it to brighten even the darkest dungeon.
A scroll that guides spirits and undead monsters to where they belong. Use it to break the curses on spirits and undead monsters and purify them.
A scroll holding a levitation spell. Use it to float every member of your party in the air, letting you walk even where there is no floor.

A scroll holding an escape spell. Use it and pure white smoke gushes from it, hiding the users from sight. The spell is magic, but the smoke is real: take the scroll out first! Use it lazily in your pocket and the air pressure will rip your clothes.

A scroll holding the power of breath. Use it and flames burst from the scroll at your foes, as powerful as a dragon's breath. It is meant to breathe fire, but not if the user has a different breath element.
A scroll holding a spell that briefly lifts range limits. Use it and your whole party's attack range becomes infinite, so now you can hit foes who felt safe out of reach.
A scroll holding a spell that raises evasion to a set level. Use it, and even the clumsiest start nimbly dodging attacks.
A scroll holding a spell that blocks level drain. Use it and a drain barrier appears before you, blocking an enemy drain attack once.
A scroll holding a spell that blocks breath. Use it and a breath barrier appears before you, blocking an enemy breath attack once.
A flute blessed by the gods. Its clear, light tone lifts the curses of the undead and spirits. Spirits purified by it are said to rise to heaven with very peaceful faces.
As its name says, the sound of its strings relaxes the listener's heart and lures them into a deep sleep. It works even if the listener is a monster.

A trumpet with no fancy tricks, made only to be loud. So loud that even someone too far off to see will hear it clearly. When it's used, the user should of course wear earplugs, and ideally their allies should too.

Bells used in the East to worship or bless the gods. Holding them, Kannagi offer dances to the gods. Their sound also forms a pure-sound barrier, briefly purifying weapons so they can strike spirits normally.
The sound of this lute charms all who hear it. At times, it is said, it steals even the player's heart.

These maracas are enchanted to amplify the rhythm they play, and can make even the quietest ally dance. Monsters will want to kill anyone dancing mid-battle first. Put the other way, you can draw the enemy's attacks onto a chosen ally.

The sound of a drum is often described as deep and rumbling in the gut, and the phrase fits perfectly. Even an ordinary drum sounds as if it could shake the ground and crack it, but this drum amplifies that power until it truly shakes the earth and splits the land.
A flute whose clear tone can return space warped by spells to normal. The effect reaches allies as well as enemies, so use it with care.

A tool that sets a reference pitch, correcting the drift in tone that creeps in with long use. This fork does more than tune: it can also restore a person's body to good health, and it does wonders for staying healthy.

Pluck the first string, and black clouds gather. The second, and heavy rain falls. The third, and thunder roars. The fourth, and divine lightning strikes. The fifth, and the foe is charred black. Pluck the last, and the foe's hair frizzes up as they breathe their last.
The Fool tarot card. These normally come as a set, so you'll almost never see a single one on its own.
The Mage tarot card. These normally come as a set, so you'll almost never see a single one on its own.
The High Priestess tarot card. These normally come as a set, so you'll almost never see a single one on its own.
The Empress tarot card. These normally come as a set, so you'll almost never see a single one on its own.
The Emperor tarot card. These normally come as a set, so you'll almost never see a single one on its own.
