A reddish ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. It is slightly softer than other ores and easily crushed to bits with a hammer or the like.
An ore of higher grade and greater value than ordinary Dvel Soft Steel. At this grade, it becomes goods you can sell to mining towns and the like.

An ore of even higher grade than Dvel Soft Steel +1, prized for its rarity. Hold it and you'll find it much heavier than plain Dvel Soft Steel; the stone's density differs. Even when making the same thing, the quality of the result varies greatly with the ore's grade.

A green ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. The ore itself gives off cold, so it is cold and hard. For that reason, scrap unfit for alchemy is used as a cooling material.
An ore of higher grade and greater value than ordinary Frozen Elven Iron. It is said that if it suddenly turns cold as you dig deeper into a mine, Frozen Elven Iron is close by.

An ore of even higher grade than Frozen Elven Iron +1, prized for its rarity. If you mean to dig up lots of Frozen Elven Iron, bring a coat into the mine. It is merely cool at first, but where it clusters in large masses, the area suddenly turns as cold as winter.
A purple ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. Its dark color makes it easy to miss when mining unless you look closely.
An ore of higher grade than ordinary Vectreim, prized for its rarity. Vectreim itself gives off an aura, but the aura can only be seen when the air around it is clear.

An ore of even higher grade than Vectreim +1, prized for its rarity. At this grade, however dark its color, the light of its aura lets you find it. Before mining starts and the dust flies, it shows quite a fine gleam.
A light-blue ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. As it is charged with magic power, it is often used in crafting meant to raise magic power.

An ore of higher grade than ordinary Mazurite, prized for its rarity. Its magic power is stronger too, and it glows a quiet blue. With a Mage in the party, you might be able to find it by sensing its magic power.

An ore of even higher grade than Mazurite +1, prized for its rarity. It holds so much magic power that only a Mage of real power can sense it. So at this level, all you can do is search as for any other ore and pray it turns up by chance.

A white ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. Split one cleanly in two and you'll see about three layers inside. The surface is white, but the color shifts toward the core with its mineral content.

An ore of higher grade than ordinary Tri-Layer Orat, prized for its rarity. Minerals settled in its core make all its layers tighter and more distinct. Despite the name, from about this grade it starts to split into more than three layers.

An ore of even higher grade than Tri-Layer Orat +1, prized for its rarity. Its minerals have settled, making it easier to use. Miners play a game with it, 'Layer Guess': from the outside of an Orat that looks like scrap, they guess the number and colors of its layers.

A milky-white ore. It can be worked into weapons and armor, or turned into various items by alchemy. Milstone calls for the most care of any ore when digging. It is delicate and crumbles at a touch, so be extra careful when digging with a pickaxe.

An ore of higher grade than ordinary Milstone, prized for its rarity. But it is twice as brittle, too. If you think you've hit a large Milstone vein, swing the pickaxe carefully. Sometimes you'll need to dig by hand.

An ore of even higher grade than Milstone +1, prized for its rarity. Young miners are often lectured, 'Dig up a Milstone +2 cleanly and you're a full-fledged miner,' but in truth that makes you not merely full-fledged, but first-rate.
A wooden coin bank. It holds a little money, and you can also throw it to deal damage matching the money inside. Save a bit day by day, and when the time comes it may help you in an unexpected way.
An iron coin bank. It holds more money than the wooden one, so throwing it promises more damage. But it hurts your wallet just as much, so don't throw it too often.

A ceramic piggy bank. Put money in and it goes 'oink.' Pray to defeat a foe, and it cries the gibberish 'Oink-oink, kill ya!', deals heavy damage and shatters in glory. It takes all your money with it, so if your servant holds the purse, beware.

"If only I had chosen a different path back then..." Surely everyone has thought that at some point. This medal grants that very wish. But a life chosen anew is not always a happy one. If you still want it, take a chance on this small possibility in your hand.

Tea leaves for brewing black tea. Brewed well, it relaxes the mind and restores a little magic power. Botch it, though, and you get tea too bitter or too weak to drink. This is one job best left to your servant.

A fruit packed with a mass of air. Take the air inside into your mouth and it supplies air, letting you act underwater. The amount of air depends on the materials and the alchemist's skill. A skilled alchemist using good materials makes underwater exploration easier.

A mysterious gem that shows the scenery around you. The view from above appears in the gem just as if an angel were looking down at you, hence its name. Among adventurers it is called an essential item.

When used, it senses the surrounding space and tells you how many 'rock' blocks are on that floor. Lords everywhere first had their alchemists make them to know their lands better for war. As the technique spread and needed no more secrecy, it at last reached the common folk.
A bell adorned with a dove. Shake it lightly and it rings with a lovely, clear tone. Monsters hate this sound, and it is said they flee headlong when they hear it.

A bell adorned with a crow. Its sound is unpleasant to people but seems quite soothing to monsters. Use it to draw monsters to you. It may seem to offer little benefit, but the rare few who make a living slaying monsters prize it.

A mysterious brush: lightly sweep it over your map, and foes beyond the doors appear on it. Knowing foes lie in ambush, you can recover your strength and go in fully prepared. Then again, try not to despair upon learning you're surrounded.

Die holding these, and you'll sit up after death and walk back to where you set out, they say. Nothing is scarier, for your killer and those you return to. With the dead really walking, ghost-story sales crashed, so 'Eastern Yokai Tales' was compiled to win them back. Hang in there, booksellers.

It won't turn in an ordinary wind. But when a monster is before you, the pinwheel starts to spin according to the monster's strength. While it turns feebly you may still be fine, but once it starts spinning furiously, get ready to run, and fast.

It turns base metals into gold, grants eternal life, draws out infinite magic power... No one knew how to make it, and guesses about the Philosopher's Stone flew far and wide, but at last it has been born here. Now, what will you use its power for?
A gauntlet that seeks to send blazing life out into the world. What sets this gauntlet aflame is not fire magic, but the 'will to live' that every living thing possesses.
A sexy dress with a plunging neckline. Whoever wears it is allowed to cast off reason and live by their heart just as it is. Some say it can even let one share one's heart with the earth itself.

A Reaper's scythe tends to be seen as an ill-omened weapon that brings death, but this scythe does not exist to end lives. It is a power wielded to restore things as they should be when someone appears who disturbs the law of life.

An oddly warped ring. You may wonder why it is so warped, but think for a moment. Tilt a cube and cast its shadow in two dimensions, and it looks warped into a rectangle or hexagon. It looks warped only in our world; to a higher being it may look beautiful and true.

Do you know the far end of time? The world after Edumo devoured it at divine command, without even space, a place that both is and is not. Last to come there is the Water of Return, returning all to nothing. Will the water in your hand someday wash all away? Swallowing joy, anger, sorrow, all.

Tokoyo is eternity, the unchanging universal. Yet no universal matter escapes time's bonds; if one exists, it is essence, not matter. All things are said to be copies of essence; the copy is what exists as matter. Then is Tokoyo essence itself, the gods' blueprint, enfolding all like gauze?

'Junk' does not mean anything in particular. It might be a bucket with no bottom, or a pen that no longer writes. One person's junk may be another's priceless treasure. In short, 'junk' is just a label for things you don't need. Got it?
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack more than a plain Fire Magic Seal. It holds a fair amount of magic, so only spellcasting classes are allowed to equip it.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack more than a plain Ice Magic Seal. It holds a fair amount of magic, so only spellcasting classes are allowed to equip it.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack more than a plain Bolt Magic Seal. It holds a fair amount of magic, so only spellcasting classes are allowed to equip it.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack even more than the Fire Magic Seal +1. It holds great power, so mastering it puts its owner's aptitude to the test.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack even more than the Ice Magic Seal +1. It holds great power, so mastering it puts its owner's aptitude to the test.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack even more than the Bolt Magic Seal +1. It holds great power, so mastering it puts its owner's aptitude to the test.
A Magic Seal that grants a Mage the greatest power. They say those without the aptitude burn to cinders just by touching it.
A Magic Seal that grants a Mage the greatest power. They say those without the aptitude turn to icicles and shatter just by touching it.
A Magic Seal that grants a Mage the greatest power. They say those without the aptitude evaporate just by touching it.

A Fairy-only dagger with a blade made of a special gem. The gem is cut so the blade resembles a petal, hence the name 'marquise.' To match, the grip is shaped like leaves. It is very beautiful to look at, and strong in battle as well.

A blade shorter than a katana but longer than a dagger. It is used mainly for self-defense or to back up a katana. But there are said to be sword styles that make the kodachi their main weapon, and its nimble blade is not to be underestimated.
A weapon said to house a demon's soul. Fighting poison with poison, perhaps, it is very effective against demons. One account holds that a powerful Summoner made it through a pact with a demon.

An eastern legend tells of a princess who couldn't be with her love; she took up this naginata, became a yasha and burned herself with them. So the lovelorn gaze at this spear in rapture. Unleash its hidden power to relive the legend. If a companion likes this spear, you'd better talk it over.
A bow whose limbs and string are partly reinforced, raising the range and power of its arrows. Compared with the Longbow, it promises steadier attacks.
A bow built to suit expert Rangers, taking in their every suggestion. It is tuned for precision over ease of handling, so beginners need not apply.

A rod known for its many different effects. Even the wielder can't tell which effect will come out, and the foe is left confused too: "Deadly poison last time, and now sleep!?" Truly a weapon fit for a fairy.

A rod made in the image of the night sky. The crystal at its tip ever turns starlight into magic power for its owner. If the sun nurtures life, moonlight and starlight nurture the heart. Close your eyes and listen closely, and you can face your own heart.

Some idiot made a boomerang out of iron, when it should be made of wood. The iron made it heavier, so its odds of coming back even after hitting something shot up. Anyone could have seen that coming. Throw with care, or your allies will boo.

As if an iron boomerang weren't dangerous enough, an even bigger idiot made one of obsidian. Its mass is ample. Its razor-sharp obsidian edges slice the foe, and it returns with its momentum intact. It's hopeless. Hide behind your Lord. Its power as a weapon? Want to know? Take a hit yourself.

Masters so skilled they were called gods of the sword were honored by pupils and peers as Sword Saints. This breastplate was a gift to them. Its defense is very high, and it never hinders the signature moves of any school of swordsmanship.
An improved form of the original Elven Chain, a chain mail whose magic defense is raised to the limit. But for all its power, only elves can equip it.

Fairy clothing made from morning glories. It takes fiddly little work to make, so fairies usually make their own. Still, dwarf craftsmen and the like sometimes make a slightly stylish version, magnifying glass in hand.

A mantle evoking the midsummer sun. Its gleaming gold brooch and fabric, thin as a curtain of light, are lovely. If a fairy in it does a little twirl, flames burst forth at once and sweep the foes away.

A talisman that repels the Kin of Darkness; Kannagi use it to defeat evil. Ordinary people and animals can touch it safely, but the Kin of Darkness vanish at its touch as if evaporating. So potent that even a non-Kannagi is warded from evil just by carrying it.
An anklet that inflicts Silence. Paired with a Ranger's First Strike, it can silence enemy magic users before they finish chanting their spells.

These dice don't foretell what will happen. They tell you why anything turned out as it did. Things often happen in this world that can only be called fate. Roll these dice, and they will show you the workings behind it.

A wand set with three kinds of gems. Most arms and armor have origins you can guess, but this wand's material and making are unknown. It looks ordinary, but dwarves say it's a material they've never seen, worked in a way they can't figure out.

A wand topped with a plush Prof. Nambino. Be invincible to magic just like Prof. Nambino~! ...Nope, not in the slightest. But with this wand, you're with Prof. Nambino anytime, anywhere! C'mon, let's go adventuring with Prof. Nambino!

A wand topped with a plush Prof. Rombino. Be invincible to physical attacks just like Prof. Rombino~! ...Nope, not in the slightest. But with this wand, you're with Prof. Rombino anytime, anywhere! Now use Prof. Rombino to squish that jerk you hate flat~!
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of light. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a Priest, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that amplifies the power of darkness. Anyone can equip it easily, but the boost is only modest. If you're a Mage, equip at least the next rank up.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack more than a plain Light Magic Seal. It holds a fair amount of magic, so only spellcasting classes are allowed to equip it.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack more than a plain Dark Magic Seal. It holds a fair amount of magic, so only spellcasting classes are allowed to equip it.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack even more than the Light Magic Seal +1. It holds great power, so mastering it puts its owner's aptitude to the test.
A Magic Seal that boosts elemental attack even more than the Dark Magic Seal +1. It holds great power, so mastering it puts its owner's aptitude to the test.
A Magic Seal that grants a Priest the greatest power. They say those without the aptitude are not even allowed to touch it.
A Magic Seal that grants a Mage the greatest power. Those without the aptitude will be swallowed by darkness and lose their souls just by touching it.

A knight's sword only men may equip. It's said that if you picture the one you must protect, the strength of that feeling becomes power. In duels to the death between knights, rarer now than they once were, it is often the weapon brought out.

A foil wrapped in silence, like a calm sea at dusk. Its supple blade shows the wielder's heart. Thrust while it sways and wavers, it does little. But when the heart is still as a calm sea, it pierces prey with ease, they say, as if striking in a world where time has stopped.
A dagger refined for dealing fatal wounds swiftly. It wasn't specially forged for strength, but it's famed for delivering blows that easily prove fatal, thanks to how easy it is to handle.

A weapon that presses a spinning blade on the foe to cut through flesh. Slash normally and you won't get the results you want. Pin the foe down hard and cut through: that is the proper way to fight with it.
A sword named 'vile blade' because it is so often used for assassination. It's inconspicuous hidden under clothes and doesn't glint needlessly, so it is very popular with those in that line of work.

Love with a spirit being rarely bears fruit, and vows to meet again are seldom kept. The snow woman is one such sad winter spirit. From the day she promises to meet again someday, she counts the falling snowflakes, awaiting her beloved.

Love with a spirit being rarely bears fruit, but some overcome many obstacles and are united. A snow woman gives this dagger to the one she means to spend her life with. Within its cold blade, you can feel a passion hot enough to melt.

A katana with the power of a mythical beast of far eastern legend. The karasu tengu is a master of sword and mystic arts. The unskilled holding it hear a strange voice coaching them in swordplay and tactics. Rare for a katana, its blade is black. One swing and a jet-black flash strikes the foe.

A katana home to a female spirit named Aramisaki. She seems to fret over being left on the shelf and is at her wits' end. So only men can hold it, and if one gets cozy with a woman, he's cursed for generations on generations, right down to the tip. A famed blade that vexes holder and held alike.
A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. But it uses tarot cards with no allegory, so don't expect much from it.

A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. Swing it and petals scatter from the blade, filling the area with cherry blossoms in full bloom, a true 'Mi-Yoshino,' fair as Yoshino itself.
A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. Its edge is even keener than that of Chaff or Fair Yoshino, with power worthy of the name 'Clearly Splendid.'
A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. It unites a boar's courage, a deer's gentleness and a butterfly's grace. A lucky sword, it is sometimes given as a gift.
A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. Its three cards, Warbler & Plum, Crane & Pine and Curtain & Cherry, are said to depict the title of a play from the eastern land.

A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. These eastern tarot have five rare 'Light' cards. Get four of them, including the one called 'Ono no Michikaze in the Willow', and you have Rainy Four Lights.
A katana with the mystic power of a tarot born in the East. Collect all five of the rare tarot cards called Light cards and you get the Five Lights.

A spear's thrust is fierce, but a dodged one leaves you wide open. Some rework the spearhead to wound the foe as much as possible; Gowen's Wringer is one. Snag even part of the foe's body, and a twist will tear away the flesh.

A spear famed among samurai. It is huge, twice a man's height. Its name comes from a tale that a dragonfly trying to land on its tip was sliced clean in two. True or not, its keen edge is beyond doubt.

An axe made more combat-ready with paired blades on either side of the haft. If one blade chips, fight on with the other. Thrown with a spin, it even works as a throwing weapon. But if that doesn't finish the foe, you face them empty-handed, so be careful.
Savage in make and in use. Even if its owner wields it normally at first, its sheer savagery slowly makes their fighting savage too.

A hammer that bends partway along its haft. A long-hafted weapon is surprisingly easy to deflect with a sword or shield. But this hammer's haft folds with a clack right where it is blocked, so it can still strike the foe.

A hammer with an oversized head holding a heavy iron ball, so each blow brings a second impact after the hammer's own. That second blow, struck with the hammer pressed to the body, travels inside to wreck and shatter bones and organs.
A mace modeled on a camel. Its knobby humps store not fat but magic power, which they absorb or release to suit the surroundings. So to some degree, this mace lets you see the flow of magic power.

Just as nations rise and fall over long history, faiths fade once no longer needed. This mace may once have been worshipped and defined an era, but now no one knows it. People cling with all their might when they need something to lean on, then toss it aside when bored. That's people for you.
A mace said to be favored by those called 'Master.' It has a wide range of uses: felling targets, repelling attackers, punishing sinners, and assorted other amusements.
A flail said to have been made by a high-ranking Priest to fight mighty spirits. It is carved with runes, and like a magnet, without any chain, it draws in anything carved with the matching rune.
A club modeled on a three-leaf clover. Unusually for a club, it values looks over power or handling, with extra care put into its decoration. Good for fighting, good for display.

A bow for Mages only. When someone with magic touches the grip, an arrow of light appears. It turns magic into matter; the arrow's hardness and accuracy are said to depend on the owner's magic. Spells alone are trouble enough. Add a bow, and they're unstoppable.
A bow that looses arrows nimbly, like a skylark's song. An easy-to-grip handle and a light build allow fine moves and rapid fire. It also allows trick shots, so it is seen in contests too.
A ribbon woven from a strange material that shines in rainbow colors. Its trail becomes a whip of light that strikes foes. Twirl it in a circle and a ring of light appears and flies at the enemy.

An ash-wood stake. Weak against ordinary creatures, but devastating to the undead. To vampires it is a dread weapon, yet also an alluring holy tool that can end an undying body. Some nobles of the night are said to be abnormally aroused by being wounded with it.

A staff made of the holy plant Welish, as is. Even worked, it stays fresh; bring your nose close to enjoy its green scent. It's edible, but very spicy, and eating it after clubbing foes gives one pause, so it isn't food except in an emergency.
A reinforced ladle. It is tougher than an ordinary ladle, and if you smack someone with a snap of the wrist, it rings out with a satisfying sound.

A rod popular for its girly design. Its basic shape and carved logo can't be changed, but the gem on the tip and such can reportedly be custom-ordered. So more than a few buy it as fashion rather than a weapon.
A weapon with blades sticking out in three directions. Among throwing weapons it is accurate, and it works well enough even without much training.
A folded crane made of steel. The steel sheets are so sharp you wonder how it was ever folded. If you don't know how to hold it, just picking it up will draw blood.

A Three-Ray Star with blades sprouting every which way. The blades vary in length and size, yet believe it or not, its center of gravity is set dead center. Its jumbled blades and spin leave the target with fine cuts that are hard to avoid.
A thick, large needle said to pierce a thousand sheets of paper. Whether it really can is unknown, but if one is thrown at you, you won't come out unscathed.

An opera libretto said to be the moon's gift to one who practiced prayer songs to it every night, for their talent. Its scales draw a Bard's vocal charm out to the limit; no ordinary composer could write it, so some say it truly came from the moon.

A frying pan reinforced with Cyclops craft. It never burns food at any heat, fries eggs without oil, and rinses clean with just water: godlike convenience. Thanks to its toughness, it also works as a shield.

A helm with mighty horns, after the black bull that charges headlong. Wearing it apparently makes you feel stronger and want to run wild. Its unmistakable look makes it popular with kids. If an adventurer dad brings this helm home, he'll be a bit of a hero that day.

A helm made from Bahamut's head, magically smoked. It turns Bahamut's immense magic power into defense, protecting its owner from foes. Some wear it as proof they slew Bahamut, to flaunt their strength.

The whiskers of Raizam, one of the Four Sages, ruler of the earth. Equip them, and even races without whiskers can feel what having them is like. But they seem itchy and unpleasant until you get used to them, so only a few oddballs wear them.

A helm with a holy blessing. Once a Lord can gather holy gear, they become aware anew that they are a 'Lord.' Until now, weren't you a Lord only because your class was Lord? But now it's different. You yourself will shape what the Lord class is.
An airy hat woven from straw. Seen in many lands, it comes in many shapes, from fashion hats to practical ones. A hat with a long history, ever loved by common folk.

Caron rarely wears hats, so this prototype was going to be scrapped. But Namina insisted it was cute, so it went on sale. Of course Namina bought one too, but always wears a particular hat for training, so it hardly ever gets used.

Hunting-tribe garb that came into use as armor. Made of game hides with little treatment, it smells a bit of blood. But it masks your own scent, so it has many fans among Rangers. Its drawback: meat-eating animals and monsters are more likely to target you.
A lavish Koinunu that, even among the hunting tribes, only chieftains may wear. Its flashy look can at times make attackers falter.

Clothes made of light, sturdy cloth so even girls can adventure with aggressive moves. The ad copy: 'Even Cerberus can't bite through it!?' Nobody has tested it, though. The claim: 'There's a ?, so it's no lie.' And it really is durable.

A historic costume made for Bards with the finest voices. It bears the 'habits' of the great Bards who wore it, so it guides the wearer's posture, and they say it lets them sing as finely as those before. It is also said to shift through seven colors with the quality of the voice.

Glove-shaped, but woven inside with steel thread for decent durability and defense. Caron's pride and joy, yet Caron reportedly moped for three days after seeing a woman in a port town using them as pot holders, perhaps a gift from her child.

Shoes made hard and sturdy to withstand intense exercise. Very water-repellent too; rumor says a well-timed kick can even deflect a mage's ice spell. The drawback: they repel water so well that ordinary washing barely gets them clean.
Yellowed fabric, peeling Emperor Bird embroidery and a strange, pungent smell all tell how old this blanket is. Anyone can see it's garbage, but to a certain someone it is apparently very precious.

An anklet wrapped in fluffy fur given a sleep effect, made from the pelt of an animal that died in hibernation. Adds sleep to any bow and arrow. It also brings its owner sound sleep; when worn, it seems to pulse faintly, thump-thump.

A weapon whose pattern works as a magic seal, adding confusion to its owner's attacks. Tracing the pattern with a finger or following it with the eye confuses anyone, owner or not, so handle it with care.

A weapon set with a charming jewel. Once the jewel enters your sight, you cannot help being charmed by its beauty. These jewels sell for high prices, but whether that is due to the charm or to honest appraisal, no one can say.

An anklet that wraps loosed arrows in vacuum blades, giving them the power to behead. Now mass-produced, but the first was said to be a wind spirit in love with an adventurer who changed form to stay with them forever. The Beheading Anklet you got... perhaps the one you hold now is 'the one'.

An anklet that senses magic and makes arrows fly straight at its source. Yuja, a witch tormented by past sins yet cursed never to die by her own hand, made it to have Polyte shoot her. Legend says Polyte's superhuman skill spared her a fatal wound, and Yuja, persuaded, set off to atone.

This shell is said to swallow nearby sound, but the sound stops because it fixes the ambient magic, briefly stilling the air. Near it, mages can't cast spells. Strictly, they do cast, but new magic can't enter the fixed space, so the spell is canceled automatically.

In a certain library, a strange bookmark placed in --- pages, or pages one must not forget, is said to ---. --- this bookmark and when the time comes you can ---, and --- is also possible. But --- varies with your feelings when you placed it, and it may even ---.

A charm blessed for family safety, success in studies and such. It is given by parents or close friends. Its power is uncertain. Still, it is a real joy when someone's care for you takes shape like this.

A charm given when one must send loved ones off to a dangerous place. Unlike the everyday charms handed out lightly, it carries the giver's earnest prayer for a safe journey. With it, your hearts will stay joined, however far apart you are.
Treasure that Leprechauns are said to keep hidden. If found, it sells for a fair price, but its true worth is said to be clear only to those with a discerning eye.

A nuisance of a banner handed out by the Dragon Lord in a certain town. Just carrying it earns you funny looks; equip it, and your social standing will plummet like a dragon descending from the heavens.
A cute little silverwork accessory. It's sold as a pierced earring, but for those who'd rather not pierce their ears, they'll make it a clip-on.

A pouch owned by Omshokopo, one of the Four Sages, master of wind. Just right for small items and well made, it would surely fetch a high price. But if an owner who got it from Omshokopo tries to part with it, it is said to turn into an owl and fly off.
A cloak owned by Radrecht, one of the Four Sages, master of fire. It holds the power of fire, and they say even the power of spirits can hardly contain its heat.
A seed you can receive from the Earth Goddess of a certain New Land. As long as you hold it and do nothing to grieve the land, the goddess's protection should keep you safe from every calamity.
A flat baked sweet. It is fairly easy to make and anyone can buy it cheaply, so it is very popular. It is also a staple on every bakery's menu.
A tiger-striped loincloth. Wearing it, you feel strength bulging through your muscles. If you pick a weapon to match, it has to be a club. Strike a cool, buff pose!

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. There are several curious designs unique to that land. Meaning could probably be found in each, but some cards honestly carry no allegory at all. That, in short, is what Chaff is.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. 'Fair Yoshino' is a phrase praising one region of a far eastern land; strictly speaking it is written 'Mi-Yoshino.' In the tarot, it is written in red on certain cards, which are said to be worth a fair amount.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. This card looks as if it could be read 'Anoyoroshi,' but the correct reading is 'Akayoroshi' (Clearly Splendid), which is said to mean 'clearly excellent.'

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. It shows bush clover and a boar. Unlike the deer and butterfly cards, nobody actually knows why the boar card is paired with bush clover. One theory says the leftovers were simply put together. Poor Mr. Boar.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. Look closely: the deer is looking away, as if ignoring you. In the East this card seems to stand for the tenth month, and the deer's pose gave rise to a word: 'ignore someone = deer of ten = shika-tou = shikato'.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. An old eastern tale says a butterfly that visits a peony turns to gold if you catch it. If that really happened, alchemists would go pale, but it's a tale full of dreams.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. Rumor has it a strange spell works only on people from the East. Chant 'Ume-ni-uguisu?' at one, and odds are they can't help answering 'Hoh-hokekyo!?' What kind of curse is it?

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. The design pairs a crane with a pine, but cranes' feet are not built to perch on pine branches, so some say the model was actually a stork, not a crane.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. Is someone holding a blossom-viewing party? Beyond the hanging curtain, the cherry trees are in full bloom. The storm of petals is inviting you, so why not drop in for a while?

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. A full moon shines beautifully over a field of pampas grass. It is elegant, yet somehow makes you feel lonely. Is this what they call wabi-sabi? Still, the dumplings are tasty enough to make you smile.

A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. The figure on it was apparently named Ono no Michikaze, but what this person did (or did wrong) has not come down to us. The figure gazes at the frog with odd intensity, so some guess this person was a frog lover or scholar.
A card Jeratan made, copying the tarot from the far East. Is the 'houou' what our world would call a phoenix? If so, it looks a bit too much like a chicken.

A sticky fluid that many monsters make inside their bodies. Each monster's is different: sometimes it is plain liquid, sometimes it is like a powerful acid that melts whatever it touches in an instant.

A sleep-inducing mist so thick you can see it. It stays afloat in the air for a long time, so it can be packed into leather bags. There is even a technique for turning the packed mist into sleeping medicine.
The fangs lining a monster's mouth. Perhaps the slight curve is a design to keep bitten flesh from getting away.
The bloodless hand peculiar to the spirits of the dead. The belief that a hand should be warm makes it feel all the colder.
A weapon beasts are born with. Most curve like hooks and are used to scratch and tear. Their tips can also dig into the ground, letting beasts run fast, among other things.

A venomous fang. It is somewhat modest in size next to other fangs, but its sharpness and killing power are vicious beyond compare. It bites and punches holes in the skin, then pumps deadly venom from its tip to weaken the prey.
A monster's tentacle. They range from slimy ones to vicious spiked ones. They are a tentacled monster's hands, and its weapons.

Rocks left untouched by human hands for ages are said to be spiritually sublimated and to hold special power. These are the rocks spirits attack with; the higher the sublimation, the more freely they can wield them.

A technique that reacts keenly to the hearts around it. If a foe feels hostility toward the user, it projects that hatred back as a psychic shockwave. The greater the foe's hatred, the stronger it gets. If you can treat all things with love, a Psi Blade will never hit you.
A blow from a tightly clenched fist is simple, yet deep. From an amateur, a normal punch might hit harder, but if someone well-built brings one down on you, be very wary.

Vines from an old tree. Their strength and power are nothing much, but their long reach lets them attack foes one-sidedly. We say 'old tree', but they are part of the monster's own body, and many reportedly get angry at being called that.
A weapon monsters are born with, mostly growing from the head. It is mainly used to charge and skewer a foe, but it can also meet your weapon to parry swords and the like.
The claws of the Kin of Darkness. Being natural, they differ little from us scratching with our nails. But the foe uses them clearly as weapons, so do not underestimate them.
Condensed water fired like a bullet. Even mere water becomes a terrifying weapon given speed and mass. A powerful monster can easily punch through plate mail with it.

A stretchy sticky thread, strong and tacky. As liquid it hardens on contact with air and grows strong like thread. The goo tingles to the touch. Not a thread you want to touch, but soaked in medicine it changes into fine thread, often used in crafts.

A claw far too sharp for an ordinary beast; one look tells you it is dangerous. Wild animals live where life and death are always side by side. Poke at one out of curiosity, and a weapon like this will beat nature's rules into your body.
A hand that radiates a dangerous will to draw you into its kind. Higher spirits are said to be not just cold: they can steal life force with a mere touch.

A technique that uses the centrifugal force of spinning to boost an attack. It says 'wheel', but there need be no wheel. You may swing a sword in a circle around yourself, or ram a foe while spinning.
The scythe of a giant mantis. How many insects has that blade hunted? You may get it by defeating its owner, but even a lifeless scythe must look like a threat to insects.

A tentacle its owner trained on purpose to attack with, until it evolved into a weapon. It hits with whip-like force, and at times even following its motion is hard. Unless you can react even when you can't read it, assume you have no chance to win.

A technique that controls the wind, makes a vacuum vortex in the air and slams it into a foe. Spirits excel at it, and once you know the magic principle it is surprisingly easy to cause. But even then it is hard to control, so we cannot master it without training.
The rich buy the fangs of large beasts as ornaments. Some adventurers make a living on contract with them, cutting the fangs off their kills to sell.
The claw of a spirit with no body. Being wounded by a spirit body your attacks can't even touch is hard to accept.

A vine covered in sharp thorns. It can be used like a spiked whip. The thorns are meant to anchor the vine and stick seeds onto birds and beasts, so once they snag, yanking them out easily wounds the prey.
A deadly kick unleashed by four-legged beasts. A bullet-like blow born of wild muscle can deal fatal damage even to a Fighter who takes it unguarded. This is the power of nature.

A fang with stronger venom and bite than a normal poison fang. It is shaped to slice wounds open, helping the venom spread. The truly dangerous ones are said to kill you if you just snag a finger on the poison fang of a slain beast.

They open and close slowly, but crustacean muscle is said to let them cut anything. They carve bone-in meat with ease; being caught bare would be deadly. Fight monsters with these carefully, or you may watch a loved one torn apart before your eyes, helpless.

A tail with a venomous stinger. Attacking with a tail is like having an extra hand. That alone is a nuisance, but it carries poison too. Even a graze is dangerous, so if your foe has one, mind your distance.
The claw of a lesser dragon. Lesser, yes, but still a dragon's claw. It is very sharp, and its strength is beyond measure. Dragon claws are often used to make weapons and armor.
A so-called tongue kiss. What effect this attack has depends on who it's used on. But no attractive partner would go smooching just anyone. The only one who would attack like this is... you-know-who.
An arm imbued with fire magic. Some are born that way; others wrap flames around it with magic. It is common among fire spirits and the like, but do not even think of copying it.
A fang that releases a nerve venom. What makes it scary is that, however bad the odds, a single bite might turn the tables. If your foe has one, be very careful.

The prow of a ghost ship. The old ship's grudge has hardened at its tip, longing for a new captain's orders. Weigh anchor! Read the charts! Hard to starboard!! Now, whoever stands in our way, with this huge prooow~~~ R-U-N T-H-E-M D-O-W-N!!

A fang that drains a foe's life force, favored by the Kin of Night. Its power is not the point: the 'act' of draining life force holds special meaning for them. They also love to enslave their prey, so many end up in their thrall.
Fangs of mighty beasts are also used as ornaments and tools of sorcery. Unlike our weapons, a beast kills to live. So the power of beast fangs is held sacred, and many seek to share in it.
The hard beak of a bird. It depends on the kind, but a truly hard one can even bore out wood.
Made of strange ice that never melts. The sword itself is very fine, high-grade even among monsters' weapons. If you equip it, bring gloves: the bitter cold could give your hands frostbite.
Both bow and arrows are silver. A loosed arrow pierces its target trailing glittering silver motes. Its accuracy is said to vary greatly with its owner's skill.
Originally a sword drawn in a painting. When the painting took on magic and began moving freely, the sword took form along with it. Now it can be swung like any ordinary sword. Strange, isn't it?
The claws of a fiend beast painted on a canvas, given form along with the beast. Rumor says their power depends on how good the painting is.
The claws of beasts that are no ordinary animals, but have gained the power of darkness. Made more savage, these fearsome claws, built for pure destruction, overwhelm adventurers.
An ogre's broadblade. Clumsy-looking, but the perfect shape for smashing with brute force. The grip is wound round and round with non-slip cloth. Grip: excellent.

Among the moves derived from the Fist is the Umeboshi, which came from the eastern land. You make fists with both hands and grind them into both of the foe's temples. On children, it is said to work wonders.
A finger shining as if divine. Its owner feels nothing, but to anyone else it is searing hot. Its normal attacks are strong, but it is vicious enough to turn a foe to stone just by pointing at them.
Ordinary tentacles move vaguely, pushed by shifting body fluids, but this one is driven by real muscle. Think it's the same as before, and a supple, lashing arm will slap you.

Fingers with a silken, finely textured touch. Their moist beauty seems to draw you in; one look is enough to make you sigh. One slinky stroke, and even the wildest brute turns meek and docile, and the loveliest flower scatters its petals amid tears of joy.

A bewitching art that lures the target with aching sighs. To get them in the mood, get in it yourself first. You mean to seduce, then fall for real... a common tale. The scary part is the cool head to kill even one you've grown fond of. If it goes badly, oh well: off to Madrie Church, go go!

Claw of a mid-ranked dragon. At this level, store-bought gear grows useless. Block with a sword and the blade chips; guard with armor and it shatters. Please do not be so arrogant as to face it head-on. Think about it: your foe is a "dragon."

A huge block of ice drifted in from cold lands. In early spring it is a seasonal sight of sorts, but heaving it up with all your might and slamming it on a foe is an attack with no poetry whatsoever. Then again, the spray can make a rainbow afterward, which is elegant in its own way.

A sword with value as an antique. Overly ornate swords can rarely be counted on as weapons, and this one is no exception. Collectors prize its age and savor the character seeping from it, but it is a little unreliable to trust your life to.

Clerics say a spirit's attack seems to wound the flesh but really strikes the soul. Life is not whittled away because the body is struck; the body crumbles because life has been whittled away. Not that it makes any difference in the end.

Shockwave attacks are not so rare, but this wave is said to carry emotions along with the shock: the anger, fear or scorn the foe feels toward you. Tossed about by those feelings, your mind and body come apart, and you can no longer move, as if paralyzed.

A rod dark jesters use to reap their prey's lives amid mocking laughter. It is said to grow ever more vicious in answer to their cruel smiles. Its power calls forth more blood and carnage, and the mad revel only speeds up.

Heels whose points are sharp as spikes, with a toughness and power you'd never guess from their elegant look. One kick easily wrecks shoddy gear. A nasty weapon... but what if you were the one wearing them? Painful, dangerous, yet beautiful...! A rose without thorns would be dull, wouldn't it?

A robe worn by liches. It is highly resistant to Dark magic. Liches already belong to darkness, and on top of that they wear robes like this, so it is no exaggeration to call using Dark magic on a lich suicide.

A scythe that strikes fear into all who see it. Most armor is weak at the joint between neck and torso. Aim for that slim gap, slip the blade in... shhk... then draw it back with a snap of the wrist, and you can harvest your foe's soul.

A bewitched spear that seeps out of shadows. As long as there is a shadow, it can strike from anywhere, which makes it a grave threat at night. Dark spirits often wield it, and that is one reason it's said you must never anger them.

Ask which fang truly has value to an adventurer, and one answer is a fang kept as proof of slaying a mighty foe. It can be a legendary beast's, or one from a foe you remember as "I'd win easily now, but back then it took everything I had." It becomes a fang in the heart that spurs adventurers on.

The claw of a stronger demon. Among the Kin of Darkness, front-line fighters likely all carry one. Even after its owner is slain, magic still lingers in the claw, and anyone weak of heart who touches it would be swallowed up in an instant.

A trident said to belong to the mermaid queen, symbol of rule over the sea. At sea, nothing can escape it. It calls whirlpools, gathers black clouds, and strikes down with lightning any who disrespect the sea. Fishermen greatly fear it for this.

A move that drives a clenched fist straight down. Simple, but the shock running from the crown down the spine is not to be taken lightly. Thrown with real hostility, it can even kill. This is no time to joke about it making you shorter.

A vine of the alraune, a bewitching flower. It looks thin, wiggly and flimsy, but it bends like a well-tanned whip and slices the skin. Even if you block it, it coils around you and pins you, so even veteran adventurers find it hard to fend off.

The scale dust that cloaks a poison moth. It may spray the dust straight at you, or flit around scattering it. It also causes hallucinations, and many adventurers who scoff at a mere bug end up losing their lives.

Claw of a high-ranked dragon. A lesser dragon's intellect is little better than a beast's, but a greater one is a match for a human at least, sometimes wiser than us. If it wields its claw's power calmly and precisely, an average adventurer stands no chance.
A fan whose wings are finished razor-sharp. Thrown well, it reportedly can part a foe's head from its body, like the 'Takasago' play in the fan-tossing game tosenkyo.

A kyosoku is an armrest from a land far to the east. Lean an elbow on it in a relaxed pose and onlookers feel awed and cowed. A must-have for court nobles. So if such a person hurls their armrest at you, they are truly furious. Short of groveling on the floor, you won't be forgiven.

A claw borne by beasts whose names are known across the land. They have evolved outside nature's laws, and the land will never make peace with them again. Yet that they survive anyway is proof of nothing but the power this claw holds.

Long ago, hearts grew desolate and the land was engulfed in war. When a king asked the dragons for help to end the strife, they gave him this Dragon Emperor Sword instead of their aid. Raise it high, and you can wield the dragons' power against the foe before you.

A strange art that calls brass-colored lightning down from the sky onto a foe at a thought. Unlike normal lightning, it does not pass through the body into the ground, but races around inside it until spent. Take a hit, and your body will be covered in worm-like burns.
Slime serves several purposes: keeping the body from drying out, helping it slide, catching prey, and so on. If you face a foe with slime, working out what it is for may lead you to victory.

A sword with an evil will. It takes over its wielder's mind and seeks ever greater power. So when it sees that a foe is stronger than its current wielder, it may even let the wielder be killed on purpose, so that the foe will pick it up.

Makes destructive waves by quivering. When a wave hits a body, it sets off resonance and destroys it from within. In theory, quivering in time with an incoming wave could amplify it and send it back, a 'wave return', but no one has pulled it off yet.

A big move: open wide and swallow the foe whole. Anyone would do it with a favorite food in front of them. Doing the eating is fine, but being gulped down to the stomach with a "Thanks for the meal!" is to be avoided at all costs.

A halo is the glow behind a holy figure. We tend to embrace things linked to what we already embrace. The Demon Halo reflects the heart of whoever faces the demon. If that heart is steeped in evil, they will bow to its evil radiance, even though the foe is a demon.
A hydra's fang. It is thicker and more firmly rooted than an ordinary snake's, so each bite really hurts. And since several heads are dealing them out, it stands to reason that hydras are strong.

A lamia's tail. Its supple muscles strike hard enough to knock a foe out in one blow. The tailed lower half is a snake's, yet it shares the human upper half's traits, so it's warm and lovely to touch or have coiled around you. Unable to forget the feel, people keep switching class to Summoner.

The fly knights ever on guard around the Insector Lord, king of the flies. Besides their king, they also guard those the king approves of. Fiercely loyal and known to see every duty through, they are feared far and wide.

A move: make a blade of your hand and bring it down on the foe's crown with a 'Hi-yah!' Done badly, it's just a chop, but they say a master's can take off a head. How does it differ from a bare-handed attack? Ask a master and you'll get 'Fool! It's different, totally different!!' So beware.

A big move that acts on the air to form a pressure fault, then shifts it, catching the foe in the friction. The victim loses balance, gripped by a strange feeling, as if upper and lower body suddenly slid apart. Go along with it, and you'll be gently twisted, swaying, and torn apart.
A beak imbued with the power of flame. If its owner wishes, whatever it pecks turns to ash. Focus flame into the beak and charge, and you can launch an attack just like a firebird.

The whip of the Hell Master, jailer of Hell. The common Hell Master is toned down in shape and power so adventurers can use it. So some adventurers are baffled by how the Hell Master's original Hell Master differs from their replica one. Of course, the genuine article is far stronger.

A fang of light that shines in rainbow colors. It is very beautiful, and depending on its clarity it can be worth more than diamonds and other gems. But each time it is used to strike a foe, its clarity drops, so very clear ones are extremely rare.

Fire too many Psi Blades (that is, be attacked by all around for too long), and in time the mind is transformed. However it is treated, it takes everything as an attack. It turns every emotion into hatred and grief and fires it: that is Psi Blade +1. If a foe fired this at you, could you take it?

An arm blazing so fiercely it could fairly be called hellfire. A weapon borne by greater spirits and the like. You feel intense heat just standing near it, so friend or foe, take care when getting close to anyone with this arm.
Not the usual swallow-whole: an improved move that unhinges the jaw like a snake to swallow prey bigger than its own mouth whole. It's fine to watch an animal do it, but...

A claw as bright red as blood. That blood-like color is in fact a paralyzing poison. When it scratches, it pours poison into the wound and paralyzes the foe. Once the victim can't move, all that's left is to surrender to the claw's owner.

A whip that only chosen demons may wield. Netherworld hellfire spews from the grip, and each lash sends sparks dancing through the air. Struck by it, you'll not only be burned, but have your very soul scraped away.

A Great Wheel spinning even faster. There are many theories on the spin path that adds most power; some say an elliptical path with a fast-slow rhythm beats a near-circular one at constant speed. Why not master the Great Wheel yourself?
The scythe of Samael, a huge mantis-like skeleton that portends death. All who meet Samael are killed, so bringing its scythe home is considered a pipe dream.
The deadly claw of beasts that have become legend. Its power is guaranteed: you will taste its destructive force, greater even than the rumors, with your own bodies.
A soul that wanders long as a wraith hones its grudge ever sharper. In time that grudge takes the form of claws, swung at the living.
A claw borne by the very highest class of dragons. Before it, ordinary armor and gear tear like paper. A legendary claw that it's said no one has ever brought back.

A saber borne by the dark knights. Strengthened by dark rites, it is tuned to bring out their full power. It can also petrify, so even blocking one blow is very dangerous. And if a high-ranking demon wields it, you had best be braced for the worst.

Claws of the very highest demons. Small as they look, they hide fearsome power within. Even a scratch could prove fatal. If you must face one, whoever first touches the other's body will be the victor.

What could be called the vessel of life for young homunculi. The flask has no special treatment, but it is reinforced by the will of the homunculi desperately guarding this home to survive. When that will breaks, their lives come to an end.
Armor painted in a picture, made real along with the monster inside it. It does have the defense its looks suggest, but no special abilities beyond that.

A vintage suit of armor. Zombie knights and armor given false life sometimes wear it, and collectors drool over it. A living suit of armor is fine, but beware a zombie knight: if one stands before you wearing this, every challenger before you has fallen.

Headgear a grown homunculus wears to stay alive. It cannot yet live by breathing, so if this flask breaks, it will suffocate and die writhing. If you see a homunculus who broke its flask by accident, call an Alchemist for it before it is too late.
This dress gently intoxicates the heart like a sweet cocktail. A woman wrapped in it tints her surroundings a soft rose with her charm and the dress's.
Holy vestments that only the chosen among the nobles of the night may wear. Should an unworthy vampire put it on by mistake, it would crumble to ash at once.
A robe imbued with the spirits' protection. Whoever wears it, that protection is granted equally. This likely stems from the fact that spirits, at root, are the land's system for circulating mana.

A cute headband made of roses. On fine days you can see alraunes making them together in high spirits. It invites sleep and confusion, so it's fine gear too. Filled with the alraunes' heartfelt care, these real roses never wither.

Mail made for the Royal Honey by its worker bees. Its materials are a complete jumble, but the special defenses they give are not to be scoffed at. When it's damaged, worker bees come and patch it up, so it always looks brand new.

A robe of humiliation sent to the defeated. No one wants to wear it, yet beaten knights nearly always don it by choice. Wearing it is a way to chasten their defeated selves and stay honest with themselves, and it carries the resolve to win next time and make the victor wear it.
A cloak adorned with rime from frozen lands. Any frozen tree will do, but lively green leaves frozen just as they were are thought best. Rime itself is rarely seen, so quality seems to vary wildly.
A breastplate for Evil alignment only. It is made for easy movement so as not to hinder its owner's attacks. Even if you aren't Evil, you'd want to try it on.

A silk robe that shines at midnight. It heightens the wearer's charm further, raising it to a beauty both graceful and alluring. Even if its wearer were one of the Kin of Darkness, you'd be entranced.

Nights when the sun does not set: such miraculous nights are called white nights. Cloth woven on a white night is said to hold the power of a sun that never sets. It offers some resistance to Priest spells.
A robe said to have been worn by the goddess who rules over serpents. Wear it, they say, and you can command every kind of snake. It also offers strong resistance to snake venom.

Armor worn by the "kings" among the Kin of Darkness who have a sovereign's makings. Lesser demons may not even know it exists, but greater demons would bow down at the mere sight of someone wearing it.

"Cheap" means shoddy or low-grade. This is armor scrapped as defective while making Iron Armor, which somehow reached the market. Armor guards your body, so every adventurer is willing to spend on it. The result: the worst armor of all, which won't sell no matter how cheap.

Armor for baptized knights of a church or temple. Its hardness as armor is mediocre, but as holy armor it wields evil-banishing power against spirits, the undead and demons. Some diehards, charmed by that power, ignore finer gear and wear Crusade Armor all their lives.
A robe made for clowns. It looks extremely flashy, making a clown's every move seem even more exaggerated and fun.

A belly dress with the midriff and chest wide open. Spells raise barriers over the bare parts, so its defense is very high, and it strongly resists Holy and Dark magic. Bodily allure has long been an offering to the god of change. So do not ogle. If you can't help it, squint.
A bucket made of tin. Surprisingly handy in all sorts of situations. Good for holding water, good for holding things, good for wearing on your head: it's at home anywhere. Truly all-purpose.

Inexperienced servants are not trusted with fine tea leaves. Being allowed to handle Greater Pekoe means nothing less than being recognized as a true servant. Fledgling servants watch their seniors handle these leaves and work hard, thinking, "Someday, me too."

A planner packed with upcoming plans: a minute-by-minute schedule in meticulous writing. Things often don't go as scheduled, but fear not. It lists what to do in every foreseeable case at every point. Even what to do if you lose this planner is written in this planner.
A breastplate made of pearl oyster shell. The sea folk work the shell with a special process to make it. Perhaps that's why it has fair resistance to Mage spells.
This breastplate is presented to a clan's chief and is worked with more care than the usual oyster one. Its resistance to Mage spells is greater too, making it formidable armor.

Armor of the frenzied. While wearing it, you can turn madness into inner strength, making your physical abilities burst into bloom. The bizarre sight sends even allies fleeing. Attacking in such a state, you throw the foe into confusion as well.
A robe trimmed with brass. Brass amplifies lightning magic, so wearing this robe raises the power of lightning spells. Watch out when a mage is wearing this robe.

Claws of the demon kings. Even a fragment holds great power, so when giving a trusted subordinate a vital mission, a king may tear off a claw for protection. Attacked with these claws, with their boundless magic, or by one holding a weapon, you are in for a hard fight.

Garb for a dark wedding. Kin of Darkness rarely wear it among themselves; it is mostly used in cursed weddings of a Kin of Darkness and a child of the land blessed by the gods. Wearing it means defying the gods and forsaking the light. If you ever do, think of a loved one's face and reconsider.

A spear born of a demon god. Its destructive power is immense; one thrust is said to bore a hole in the earth. Forged with a grudge against the gods, it will show terrifying power if ever turned against a god.
'Heartbreak' means lost love. This sword seduces and tames a foe, then finishes off that love with treatment so cruel it shatters the heart. A terrifying weapon that deals huge mental damage.

A robe of daring, skin-baring design that stirs lewd, extreme urges in all who see it and makes them act on instinct. Chaos reigns around the wearer, who will suffer too. Yet once tasted, that decadent feast of madness can never be forgotten, and is craved again and again.
A terrifying dagger that slashes again, and again, and again, and again, and again, until the foe falls in a sea of blood. It is highly lethal and highly accurate.

An assassin's blade. Its accuracy is low, but a mere graze can deal a fatal wound, which makes it gear for experts. A novice flailing it about is no threat, but when a veteran draws it, never take your eyes off their hands.

The loneliness swirling in a heart, given form. Binding the body with a sash, something other than oneself, lets one feel that one is truly here. Loneliness never filled craves an ever tighter bind. This sealing sash will never tear, however tightly it binds.

A great scythe that bears the name of the crescent moon. It is said to be sharp enough to slice even the stars in the night sky. Its edge is so keen that when it is swung swiftly, it takes a moment before you notice you've been cut.
Cute clothing shaped like a pumpkin. It is all fluffy, and is said to show its full power when worn by a small child.

A buckler carried by Abi. "Shield in the right hand! Shield in the left too, that's double! Raise them by the face, five times! Run, ten times! Total: a hundred times the defense!" So Abi cried when cornered, and charged to the front line.

A shield carried by Abi. Abi's theory made little sense, and even if defense really rose a hundredfold, no fight is won by defending alone. Abi only realized this when the enemy copied the trick and gave chase.

The tentacles so far were their owners' own reinforced flesh, born with them, but this Death Tentacle is different. It has a clear will of darkness; its very existence must not be allowed. If one ever appears on your land, take it as a clear sign of invasion by the Kin of Darkness.

The fist is interpreted in many ways; thunder is often called "the fist of the gods". Indeed, perhaps only the gods can bring down a parent's fist on humans and elves in this land. But if a fist of divine wrath truly fell, we could only run away like babies.
Some oozes are strongly acidic. Doused in one, armor melts and skin festers. Just how monsters keep such ooze inside their bodies is a fascinating question.

Light hitting a gem normally reflects and escapes as sparkle. But tweak that reflection with magic, and light can get in but not out. Give the light raging inside the gem one exit, and it will burst out as a single spear of light.

Thwack, thwack! The merciless slap of Demon Duke Nyoppurin. Take one and watch out: the backhand brings a second. But don't be amazed yet. Nyoppurin can also spin with arms spread wide and deliver a tornado of slaps that leaves you no time to breathe.
It is said that, very rarely, someone bearing this factor is found in the land. How the factor arises, and what purpose it serves, are both unknown.

A huge, hard, bullet-like rock gouged into a strange shape. Its nature changes with its maker's will: it can harden further or explode on impact as needed. But scarier than any trick is the plain attack of giant rocks raining down like hail.

The most famous axe among the Kin of Darkness. The name Baltagias was fairly well known before, but it grew far more famous once Dalisiamarte, the current head of the house, won many feats of arms with this axe.

Cannibalism is humans eating human flesh; in a broad sense, any eating of one's own kind. This is a ceremonial sword used to commit that cursed act. Ceremonial or not, its shape is ideal for butchering a human body, and so it is highly lethal as well.

Battle garb made more to fire up the spirit than to protect. In a trance of blood and slaughter, you won't even mind the blows you take. In fact, you will likely feel joy and pleasure even at the blood spurting from your own body.

Armor said to guard its wearer, its defense growing with the strength of the oath held in the heart. But should the heart waver or the oath be broken, the breastplate will lose its defense. For this reason, its wearers are sometimes viewed with respect.
A claw turned white like marble. Whether from grooming or by nature is unknown, but it stands out among the claws of all races.
A bow possessed by the grudge of a beast of darkness. The grudge flies with each arrow; to the one shot, it looks like a savage beast flying at them, fangs bared.

A novice clown's outfit must look funny to make up for lacking skill. A seasoned clown, though, can create humor from within without relying on looks. So this outfit is tailored for ease of movement rather than a funny look.
A spear spoken of among the Kin of Darkness as a famed lance. It never breaks, and it is said that gripping it lets you feel the thoughts of its past owners.

The robe worn by the king of the netherworld. The whole robe is wrapped in darkness, and looking at it feels like being drawn into the dark. In fact, surrender to that feeling and your soul is said to be torn out and taken to the netherworld.
A Chopper Sword customized to order, and with great success: it now has even more attack power. Its power is off the charts, its edge is off the charts, everything about it is off the charts.

The scythe of the librarian Samariel, who looks very much like Samael. Librarians take the forms of creatures that live on the lands, the Wastelands included. Why they do so is unknown, but as befits Samael's likeness, its scythe is just as sharp. One sweep can take every head in the front row.

Slimy stuff feels awful stuck to your clothes or body. But if you give in, thinking "Oh, whatever," the discomfort turns dramatically into pleasure. Why not stop resisting and accept it just once? No responsibility taken if you can't come back from that world, though.
Unlike an ordinary snowball, it is packed hard with magic, so it can withstand a fair amount of heat. If one is thrown at you, think less "hard snowball" and more "fist-sized rock".
Moisture in the air hardened into an arrow. Mages can produce similar ice arrows too, but snow spirits are said to fire five or six at once without even trying.

Water offers great resistance, so fish in it are surprisingly strong. This is the deadly move they devised: deftly using tail and fins, they knock a foe up, then smack the falling body sideways. Fishermen know its power; with a green captain, you'll see them pop off the deck one after another.

A cruel move that crushes a foe under a huge foot. It looks like slow motion to an onlooker, but when targeted, your body freezes and you can't get away. And some stomps, even by feet of normal size, are said to inflict mental torment: fear and humiliation.

A costume for celebs, brought from a land far to the east. Many robes of different colors are layered so the colors show as stripes at the hem. But get carried away and pile on too many, and their weight will leave you unable to move, so beware.

A hooked-claw weapon made of bronze. Some are worn on the hand like gloves, but a monster's is usually part of its body. With the hardness of metal and a talon shape modeled on birds of prey, it can rip prey to shreds at will.

A heavy blow from a bronze foot. Rather than kick damage, it is built to "break" things through impact. The more precise and delicate the target, the greater the threat a Bronze Kick poses... Like, say, the human body.
A very sturdy, hard club. Get hit in the wrong spot and you'll pass out, no trouble at all.
A club studded here and there with nails and the like for extra killing power. Get hit and you'll be bloodied and off to heaven, nice and easy.

The student handbook issued at Rubenburg. It sets out a mage's precepts in three scripts: Common, Ritual Magic and Spirit. Students learn the scripts year by year in class, and read the precepts their power calls for. It shows the forebears' care: too strict or too lax won't do.
A simple baked sweet made of flour, butter, salt and sugar. Sometimes lemon or cocoa is added. Add a cup of black tea, and a little tea party begins.

Sweet bread: dough rolled into a spiral shell and baked, then filled with chocolate or cream. Whether to eat it from the wide open end or from the narrow tip depends on the person. At the Magic School it is a common sample topic in debate class.

A cake devised by someone named Mont Blanc. It uses chestnuts: whipped cream on a cupcake, then chestnut cream squeezed round and round on top. When squeezing it out, try to keep the line as thin as you can. An odd thickness will kill everyone's appetite.

The way to solve Beldoll, long thought unsolvable: in other words, its Last Theorem. A few people are said to have obtained it, yet strangely none of them ever wrote it down. Rumor even says Beldoll silences them. Will you try to put this theorem on record?
A chakram born from the blanks in history and its records. The deeper the mystery, the greater its power grows. As long as the mystery stays a mystery, this weapon will never lose its power.

A book on what a king must know to rise in the world of darkness. It details how to handle monster underlings, rewards and punishments that work, how to unite one's kin, what leadership is, and more. Read it and you'll find they worry and struggle over the same things we do.

Peer through the ring atop this staff, and it is said you can see past events that happened in that place. Lost records and the truth of history may teach you awkward facts you 'would rather not have known.' If your mind is strong enough to bear them, take a look.

A shockwave born of the elegant air a noble lady carries. The poor, of course, and even the moderately rich are said to be unable to move before its might. Yet what truly makes a lady a lady is nothing but the regal majesty she was born with.
Wings that not only fly but also create shock waves when flapped. Their colors and looks vary: wings like a bird of prey's, bat wings evoking the Kin of Darkness, beautiful pure-white wings and more.

Coveted by felines the world over. Merely holding it feels like being wrapped in catnip and brings a smile of pure bliss. It satisfies so fully that one loses the will to do anything, and many have collapsed where they stood. Staying sane once you have it takes great magic power.

At dusk, the demon hour, when gloom veils the land, the line between this world and the next is said to blur. This voice is said to be the call the 'Abyss' sends then to draw lost souls; a spirit that hears it is swallowed at once. Hear it in the flesh, and your soul will slip out, leaving a husk.
The roar that one once worshipped as a god let loose at a true god. It is so full of hatred and curses that hearing it nearby makes you shudder, even though you are not the one being blamed.

A pole axe with blades at both ends, made of a very heavy ore; just raising it is hard labor. Unless you are strong enough to wield it freely, you must keep it spinning like a windmill to fend off nimble weapons. But once it gets going it won't easily stop, so the foe can only run.

A large gem cherished by Harz, a young lady of the Kin of Darkness and Zoze's daughter. It has been part of her since birth, they say, and she has lovingly stroked it since she was small. By chance Mirco touched it; unable to forget the thrill, she began chasing Mirco around.
The mightiest swallow-whole, warping space to gulp down even things too big to swallow. Once targeted, there is next to no escape.

A grenade Professor Harmoni put heart and soul into. Its power is no joke: it can blow away a building, grounds and all. The Professor will hardly ever use it, but know its dangers well. In rock-paper-scissors it counts as dynamite; it supposedly beats rock, scissors and paper. Is that true?

Wasabi is a spice from the East, but it stings the nose more than the tongue, and differs a bit from what we eat daily. The sting can apparently be eased by breathing in through the nose. As for what role wasabi plays as a war banner, that's a long story, so let's save it for another time.

A war banner inscribed with the teaching "Strike the foe swift as lightning." The larger an army grows, the less mobile it becomes. The Hatamoto, a unit's leader so to speak, must deal properly with such problems too.

A superhuman knee strike unleashed with genius flair. Its reach is long: at any opening, the user dashes in, steps up on the foe's body and delivers a humiliating knee. Truly a flash of a move, but it takes either the ultimate body or levitation magic adapted for speed.
The horn of a unicorn, ruler of purity. Hard to obtain, but it glows faintly even in darkness and is so beautiful it is highly prized as an antique. Since it is only the horn, anyone can touch it.

The horn of a bicorn, ruler of impurity. Bicorns are thought to be foes of unicorns, but some say a unicorn is a young bicorn that grows horns as it matures: the unicorn gave up understanding for purity, the bicorn knew the world at the cost of impurity. But is it true?
The umbrella the dream demon Lukoje loves to use. It can thrust like a spear in battle, but here one would rather use it elegantly, as a parasol.

House Lenzer keeps its own smiths, and every weapon they forge for the head of the house or the family bears the name 'Baltagias.' This sword is one of them, but it was made for the young heir, so it has little power.

The demon sword Baltagias, its true power unleashed after it accepted its wielder and sought to answer the wielder's will. With power worthy of the name Baltagias, it shows the glory of House Lenzer to every world.

A whip for drilling manners into children of good families. Unlike a normal whip, it is shaped like a springy rod. A snappy blow is a real menace to a child, and can scar them for life. But if the wielder is attractive or worthy of respect, that strictness can be felt as love, they say.

Wrath is not a negative emotion. It is the noble heart that stakes everything to see its will through when one's reason to exist and beliefs are trampled. Those who call wrath evil merely lack the strength and conviction to be angry.

An earring that, when its owner is about to weep, quietly catches the tears in its gem where no one can see. Those who cannot show tears. Those who cannot let sorrow show, to protect themselves. It is said to save such hearts. Yet some sorrows are too great even for the Earring of Sorrow.

A leotard steeped in the pleasure of destruction. The snug fabric clings to the skin with a suction-like fit, so much so that you could think you were wearing nothing. That strange feeling brings an even greater thrill.

A leg of Shirinmorin, one of the Four Sages, ruler of water. Equip it and you can move it at will. You may picture holding it, but it can be attached right to your body and made part of it. Done well, you share nerves with it and swing it around like your own limb, quite literally.
A rod in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?
A hat in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?
An outfit in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?
Gloves in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?
Shoes in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?
An accessory in development at the Caron Main Store. What will the finished product be like?

A sword Undine holds dear. Only a knight she has opened her heart to may wield it. The water clan cherishes Undine; should anyone make her cry, the whole clan will come for revenge. Do you have the heart to answer her devotion?
